people.summary: Tent of the father, an artist of the tribe of Dan, appointed to the work of preparing materials for the tabernacle (Ex. 31:6; 35:34; 36:1, 2; 38:23).

people.name: Aholibah
people.summary: My tent is in her, the name of an imaginary harlot, applied symbolically to Jerusalem, because she had abandoned the worship of the true God and given herself up to the idolatries of foreign nations.

people.name: Aholibamah
people.summary: Jewess, the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and one of Esau’s wives (Gen. 26:34), elsewhere called Aholibamah (36:2-14).

people.name: Akkub
people.summary: A Levite who kept the gate of the temple after the return from Babylon (1 Chr. 9:17; Ezra 2:42; Neh. 7:45).

people.name: Ammishaddai
people.summary: People of the Almighty, the father of Ahiezer, who was chief of the Danites at the time of the Exodus (Num. 1:12; 2:25).

people.name: Ananias
people.summary: A Christian at Damascus (Acts 9:10). He became Paul’s instructor; but when or by what means he himself became a Christian we have no information.

people.name: Aristarchus
people.summary: Best ruler, native of Thessalonica (Acts 20:4), a companion of Paul (Acts 19:29; 27:2).

people.name: Asshur
people.summary: Second son of Shem (Gen. 10:22; 1 Chr. 1:17). He went from the land of Shinar and built Nineveh, etc. (Gen. 10:11, 12). He probably gave his name to Assyria, which is the usual translation of the word, although the form Asshur is sometimes retained (Num. 24:22, 24; Ezek. 27:23, etc.).

people.name: Azariah
people.summary: The original name of Abed-nego (Dan. 1:6, 7, 11, 16).

people.name: Benaiah
people.summary: A musical Levite (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

people.name: Beriah
people.summary: One of Asher’s four sons, and father of Heber (Gen. 46:17).

people.name: Bildad
people.summary: Son of contention, one of Job’s friends. He is called “the Shuhite,” probably as belonging to Shuah, a district in Arabia, in which Shuah, the sixth son of Abraham by Keturah, settled (Gen. 25:2).

people.name: Chedorlaomer
people.summary: (= Khudur-Lagamar of the inscriptions), king of Elam. Many centuries before the age of Abraham, Canaan and even the Sinaitic peninsula had been conquered by Babylonian kings, and in the time of Abraham himself Babylonia was ruled by a dynasty which claimed sovereignity over Syria and Palestine.

people.name: Cushi
people.summary: Then Joab said to a Cushite.

people.name: Daughter of Pharaoh
people.summary: The wife of Solomon (1 Kings 3:1).

people.name: Diana
people.summary: So called by the Romans; called Artemis by the Greeks, the “great” goddess worshipped among heathen nations under various modifications. Her most noted temple was that at Ephesus.

people.name: Dishan
people.summary: Antelope, the youngest son of Seir the Horite, head of one of the tribes of Idumaea (Gen. 36:21, 28, 30).

people.name: Ebed
people.summary: Slave, the father of Gaal, in whom the men of Shechem “put confidence” in their conspiracy against Abimelech (Judg. 9:26, 26, 30, 31).

people.name: Ebiasaph
people.summary: Father of gathering; the gatherer, the youngest of the three sons of Korah the Levite, head of a family of Korhites (Ex. 6:24); called Ebisaph (1 Chr. 6:37).

people.name: Eliab
people.summary: A Reubenite, son of Pallu (Num. 16:1, 12; 26:8, 9; Deut. 11:6).

people.name: Eliab
people.summary: Son of Kohath.

people.name: Eliasaph
people.summary: Prince of the Gershonites.

people.name: Ezer
people.summary: One of the sons of Seir, the native princes, “dukes,” of Mount Hor (Gen. 36:21, 27).

people.name: Gamaliel
people.summary: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh at the census at Sinai (Num. 1:10; 2:20; 7:54, 59).

people.name: Gershom
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Moses born to him in Midian (Ex. 2:22; 18:3). On his way to Egypt with his family, in obedience to the command of the Lord, Moses was attacked by a sudden and dangerous illness (4:24-26), which Zipporah his wife believed to have been sent because he had neglected to circumcise his son.

people.name: Gomer
people.summary: The eldest son of Japheth, and father of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah (Gen. 10:2, 3), whose descendants formed the principal branch of the population of South-eastern Europe.

people.name: Hadad
people.summary: One of “the king’s seed in Edom.” He fled into Egypt, where he married the sister of Pharaoh’s wife (1 Kings 11:14-22).

people.name: Haggith
people.summary: Festive; the dancer, a wife of David and the mother of Adonijah (2 Sam. 3:4; 1 Kings 1:5, 11; 2:13; 1 Chr. 3:2), who, like Absalom, was famed for his beauty.

people.name: Hammedatha
people.summary: Father of Haman, designated usually “the Agagite” (Esther 3:1, 10; 8:5).

people.name: Hanani
people.summary: A prophet who was sent to rebuke king Asa for entering into a league with Benhadad I., king of Syria, against Judah (2 Chr. 16:1-10).

people.name: Haran
people.summary: Heb. haran; i.e., “mountaineer.” The eldest son of Terah, brother of Abraham and Nahor, and father of Lot, Milcah, and Iscah.

people.name: Harim
people.summary: The head of the second course of priests (1 Chr. 24:8).

people.name: Helon
people.summary: Strong, father of Eliab, who was “captain of the children of Zebulun” (Num. 1:9; 2:7).

people.name: Hepher
people.summary: The youngest son of Gilead (Num. 26:32; 27:1).

people.name: Hezron
people.summary: One of the sons of Reuben (Gen. 46:9; Ex. 6:14).

people.name: Hilkiah
people.summary: The father of Eliakim (2 Kings 18:18, 26, 37).

people.name: Hiram
people.summary: The “master workman” whom Hiram sent to Solomon. He was the son of a widow of Dan, and of a Tyrian father. In 2 Chr. 2:13 “Huram my father” should be Huram Abi, the word “Abi” (rendered here “my father”) being regarded as a proper name, or it may perhaps be a title of distinction given to Huram, and equivalent to “master.”

people.name: Hophni
people.summary: Pugilist or client, one of the two sons of Eli, the high priest (1 Sam. 1:3; 2:34), who, because he was “very old,” resigned to them the active duties of his office.

people.name: Immer
people.summary: The head of the sixteenth priestly order (1 Chr. 24:14).

people.name: James
people.summary: The son of Alphaeus, or Cleopas, “the brother” or near kinsman or cousin of our Lord (Gal. 1:18, 19), called James “the Less,” or “the Little,” probably because he was of low stature.

people.name: Jason
people.summary: He that will cure, the host of Paul and Silas in Thessalonica. The Jews assaulted his house in order to seize Paul, but failing to find him, they dragged Jason before the ruler of the city (Acts 17:5-9).

people.name: Jehu
people.summary: The son of Hanani, a prophet of Judah (1 Kings 16:1, 7; 2 Chr. 19:2; 20:34), who pronounced the sentence of God against Baasha, the king of Israel.

people.name: Kenaz
people.summary: Caleb’s younger brother, and father of Othniel (Josh. 15:17), whose family was of importance in Israel down to the time of David (1 Chr. 27:15).

people.name: Lebbaeus
people.summary: Breast, the name of one of the apostles (Mark 3:18), called “Lebbaeus” in Matt. 10:3, and in Luke 6:16, “Judas the brother of James;” while John (14:22), probably referring to the same person, speaks of “Judas, not Iscariot.”

people.name: Lotan
people.summary: Coverer, one of the sons of Seir, the Horite (Gen. 36:20, 29).

people.name: Magog
people.summary: Region of Gog, the second of the “sons” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2; 1 Chr. 1:5). In Ezekiel (38:2; 39:6) it is the name of a nation, probably some Scythian or Tartar tribe descended from Japheth.

people.name: Mattithiah
people.summary: One of the sons of Jeduthun (1 Chr. 25:3, 21).

people.name: Meshelemiah
people.summary: Friendship of Jehovah, a Levite of the family of the Korhites, called also Shelemiah (1 Chr. 9:21; 26:1, 2, 9, 14).

people.name: Michael
people.summary: The title given to one of the chief angels (Dan. 10:13, 21; 12:1). He had special charge of Israel as a nation. He disputed with Satan (Jude 1:9) about the body of Moses.

people.name: Nathan
people.summary: A son of David, by Bathsheba (2 Sam. 5:14), whose name appears in the genealogy of Mary, the mother of our Lord (Luke 3:31).

people.name: Nebajoth
people.summary: Ishmael’s eldest son (Gen. 25:13), and the prince of an Israelitish tribe (16).

people.name: Nehemiah
people.summary: The son of Hachaliah (Neh. 1:1), and probably of the tribe of Judah. His family must have belonged to Jerusalem (Neh. 2:3). He was one of the “Jews of the dispersion,” and in his youth was appointed to the important office of royal cup-bearer at the palace of Shushan.

people.name: Nethaneel
people.summary: The son of Zuar, chief of the tribe of Issachar at the Exodus (Num. 1:8; 2:5).

people.name: Nicodemus
people.summary: The people is victor, a Pharisee and a member of the Sanhedrin. He is first noticed as visiting Jesus by night (John 3:1-21) for the purpose of learning more of his doctrines, which our Lord then unfolded to him, giving prominence to the necessity of being “born again.”

people.name: Nimshi
people.summary: Saved.

people.name: Pagiel
people.summary: God allots, a prince of the tribe of Asher (Num. 1:13), in the wilderness.

people.name: Pallu
people.summary: Separated, the second son of Reuben (1 Chr. 5:3); called Phallu, Gen. 46:9.

people.name: Pashur
people.summary: Son of Malchiah.

people.name: Pedahzur
people.summary: Rock of redemption, the father of Gamaliel and prince of Manasseh at the time of the Exodus (Num. 1:10; 2:20).

people.name: Pharaoh
people.summary: The “new king who knew not Joseph” (Ex. 1:8-22) has been generally supposed to have been Aahmes I., or Amosis, as he is called by Josephus.

people.name: Pharaoh
people.summary: Pharaoh, in whom Hezekiah put his trust in his war against Sennacherib (2 Kings 18:21).

people.name: Rehum
people.summary: One of “the children of the province” who returned from the Captivity (Ezra 2:2); the same as “Nehum” (Neh. 7:7).

people.name: Seraiah
people.summary: A ruler of the temple (Neh. 11:11).

people.name: Shallum
people.summary: Son of Zadok.

people.name: Shallum
people.summary: A keeper of the gate in the reign of David (1 Chr. 9:17).

people.name: Shammah
people.summary: One of the sons of Jesse (1 Sam. 16:9).

people.name: Shemaiah
people.summary: A prophet in the reign of Rehoboam (1 Kings 12:22-24).

people.name: Sherebiah
people.summary: Levi.

people.name: Shobal
people.summary: The second son of Seir the Horite; one of the Horite “dukes” (Gen. 36:20).

people.name: Sibbechai
people.summary: The Lord sustains, one of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:29), general of the eighth division of the army (27:11). He slew the giant Saph in the battle of Gob (2 Sam. 21:18; R.V., “Sibbechai”).

people.name: Talmon
people.summary: A Levite porter (1 Chr. 9:17; Neh. 11:19).

people.name: Tirzah
people.summary: The youngest of Zelophehad’s five daughters (Num. 26:33; Josh. 17:3).

people.name: Tychicus
people.summary: Chance, an Asiatic Christian, a “faithful minister in the Lord” (Eph. 6:21, 22), who, with Trophimus, accompanied Paul on a part of his journey from Macedonia to Jerusalem (Acts 20:4).

people.name: Uri
people.summary: Tribe of Judah.

people.name: Urijah
people.summary: A high priest in the time of Ahaz (2 Kings 16:10-16), at whose bidding he constructed an idolatrous altar like one the king had seen at Damascus, to be set up instead of the brazen altar.

people.name: Zebul
people.summary: Habitation, the governor of Shechem under Abimelech (Judg. 9:28, 30, 36). He informed his master of the intention of the people of Shechem to transfer their allegiance to the Hivite tribe of Hamor.

people.name: Zedekiah
people.summary: The son of Chenaanah, a false prophet in the days of Ahab (1 Kings 22:11, 24; 2 Chr. 18:10, 23).

people.name: Zurishaddai
people.summary: Rock of the Almighty, the father of Shelumiel, who was chief of the tribe of Simeon when Israel was encamped at Sinai (Num. 1:6; 2:12).

people.name: Abiezer
people.summary: The second of the three sons of Hammoleketh, the sister of Gilead. He was the grandson of Manasseh (1 Chr. 7:18). From his family Gideon sprang (Josh. 17:2; comp. Judg. 6:34; 8:2).

people.name: Abinadab
people.summary: A Levite of Kirjath-jearim, in whose house the ark of the covenant was deposited after having been brought back from the land of the Philistines (1 Sam. 7:1).

people.name: Abinoam
people.summary: Father of kindness, the father of Barak (Judg. 4:6; 5:1).

people.name: Abishua
people.summary: The son of Phinehas the high priest (1 Chr. 6:4, 5, 50; Ezra 7:5).

people.name: Achsah
people.summary: Anklet, Caleb’s only daughter (1 Chr. 2:49). She was offered in marriage to the man who would lead an attack on the city of Debir, or Kirjath-sepher.

people.name: Ahaz
people.summary: A grandson of Jonathan (1 Chr. 8:35; 9:42).

people.name: Ahijah
people.summary: Baasha.

people.name: Alphaeus
people.summary: The father of James the Less, the apostle and writer of the epistle (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18; Luke 6:15; Acts 1:13), and the husband of Mary (John 19:25).

people.name: Amorite
people.summary: Highlanders, or hillmen, the name given to the descendants of one of the sons of Canaan (Gen. 14:7), called Amurra or Amurri in the Assyrian and Egyptian inscriptions.

people.name: Annas
people.summary: Was high priest A.D. 7-14. In A.D. 25 Caiaphas, who had married the daughter of Annas (John 18:13), was raised to that office, and probably Annas was now made president of the Sanhedrim, or deputy or coadjutor of the high priest, and thus was also called high priest along with Caiaphas (Luke 3:2).

people.name: Azariah
people.summary: Father of Johanan.

people.name: Azel
people.summary: Noble, a descendant of king Saul (1 Chr. 8:37; 9:43, 44).

people.name: Baal-hanan
people.summary: A king of Edom, son of Achbor (Gen. 36:38, 39; 1 Chr. 1:49, 50).

people.name: Baal-zebub
people.summary: Fly-lord, the god of the Philistines at Ekron (2 Kings 1:2, 3, 16). This name was given to the god because he was supposed to be able to avert the plague of flies which in that region was to be feared.

people.name: Baanah
people.summary: One of the two sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, a captain in Saul’s army.

people.name: Bartholomew
people.summary: Son of Tolmai, one of the twelve apostles (Matt. 10:3; Acts 1:13); generally supposed to have been the same as Nathanael. In the synoptic gospels Philip and Bartholomew are always mentioned together, while Nathanael is never mentioned; in the fourth gospel, on the other hand, Philip and Nathanael are similarly mentioned together, but nothing is said of Bartholomew.

people.name: Bela
people.summary: The son of Beor, and a king of Edom (Gen. 36:32, 33; 1 Chr. 1:43).

people.name: Ben-hadad
people.summary: King of Damascus, and successor of his father Hazael on the throne of Syria (2 Kings 13:3, 4).

people.name: Carmi
people.summary: The last named of the four sons of Reuben (Gen. 46:9).

people.name: Chenaanah
people.summary: The father of Zedekiah (1 Kings 22:11, 24).

people.name: Dishon
people.summary: Duke of Horites.

people.name: Doeg
people.summary: Fearful, an Edomite, the chief overseer of Saul’s flocks (1 Sam. 21:7). At the command of Saul he slew the high priest Ahimelech at Nob, together with all the priests to the number of eighty-five persons.

people.name: Eglon
people.summary: Chieftain or king of one of the Moabite tribes (Judg. 3:12-14). Having entered into an alliance with Ammon and Amalek, he overran the trans-Jordanic region, and then crossing the Jordan, seized on Jericho, the “city of palm trees,” which had been by this time rebuilt, but not as a fortress.

people.name: Elah
people.summary: The son and successor of Baasha, king of Israel (1 Kings 16:8-10). He was killed while drunk by Zimri, one of the captains of his chariots, and was the last king of the line of Baasha.

people.name: Elah
people.summary: The father of Hoshea, the last king of Israel (2 Kings 15:30; 17:1).

people.name: Eliashib
people.summary: A high priest in the time of Ezra and Nehemiah (Neh. 12:22, 23). He rebuilt the eastern city wall (3:1), his own mansion being in that quarter, on the ridge Ophel (3:20, 21).

people.name: Eliezer
people.summary: One of the two sons of Moses, born during his sojourn in Midian (Ex. 18:4; 1 Chr. 23:15, 17). He remained with his mother and brother Gershom with Jethro when Moses returned to Egypt.

people.name: Ephratah
people.summary: The second wife of Caleb, the son of Hezron, mother of Hur, and grandmother of Caleb, who was one of those that were sent to spy the land (1 Chr. 2:19, 50).

people.name: Eve
people.summary: Life; living, the name given by Adam to his wife (Gen. 3:20; 4:1). The account of her creation is given in Gen. 2:21, 22. The Creator, by declaring that it was not good for man to be alone, and by creating for him a suitable companion, gave sanction to monogamy.

people.name: Gabriel
people.summary: Champion of God, used as a proper name to designate the angel who was sent to Daniel (8:16) to explain the vision of the ram and the he-goat, and to communicate the prediction of the seventy weeks (Dan. 9:21-27).

people.name: Gemariah
people.summary: The son of Shaphan, and one of the Levites of the temple in the time of Jehoiakim (Jer. 36:10; 2 Kings 22:12). Baruch read aloud to the people from Gemariah’s chamber, and again in the hearing of Gemariah and other scribes, the prophecies of Jeremiah (Jer. 36:11-20), which filled him with terror.

people.name: Gera
people.summary: The father of Shimei, who so grossly abused David (2 Sam. 16:5; 19:16, 18).

people.name: Geshem
people.summary: Or Gashmu, firmness, probably chief of the Arabs south of Palestine, one of the enemies of the Jews after the return from Babylon (Neh. 2:19; 6:1, 2).

people.name: Hadad
people.summary: An Edomite king who defeated the Midianites (Gen. 36:35; 1 Chr. 1:46).

people.name: Hanameel
people.summary: Whom God has graciously given, the cousin of Jeremiah, to whom he sold the field he possessed in Anathoth, before the siege of Jerusalem (Jer. 32:6-12).

people.name: Hashabiah
people.summary: One of the chief priests in the time of Ezra (Ezra 8:24).

people.name: Hatach
people.summary: Verity, one of the eunuchs or chamberlains in the palace of Ahasuerus (Esther 4:5, 6, 9, 10).

people.name: Heber
people.summary: The Kenite (Judg. 4:11, 17; 5:24), a descendant of Hobab.

people.name: Herodias
people.summary: (Matt. 14:3-11; Mark 6:17-28; Luke 3:19), the daughter of Aristobulus and Bernice. While residing at Rome with her husband Herod Philip I. and her daughter, Herod Antipas fell in with her during one of his journeys to that city.

people.name: Hoglah
people.summary: Partridge, one of the daughters of Zelophehad the Gileadite, to whom portions were assigned by Moses (Num. 26:33; 27:1; 36:11).

people.name: Hosah
people.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 16:38).

people.name: Imla
people.summary: Replenisher, the father of Micaiah the prophet (2 Chr. 18:7, 8).

people.name: Jaalam
people.summary: Concealer, the second of Esau’s three sons by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:5, 14).

people.name: Jachin
people.summary: The fourth son of Simeon (Gen. 46:10), called also Jarib (1 Chr. 4:24).

people.name: Jair
people.summary: Was the son of Segub of the tribe of Judah – Segub being a son of Hezron who married a daughter of Machir.

people.name: Jamin
people.summary: The Jaminite clan.

people.name: Jedaiah
people.summary: A priest in Jerusalem after the Exile (1 Chr. 9:10).

people.name: Jehiel
people.summary: The sons of Ladan.

people.name: Jehoshaphat
people.summary: Son of Ahilud, “recorder” or annalist under David and Solomon (2 Sam. 8:16), a state officer of high rank, chancellor or vizier of the kingdom.

people.name: Jeiel
people.summary: One of the Levites who took part in praising God on the removal of the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 16:5).

people.name: Jemuel
people.summary: One of Simeon’s five sons (1 Chr. 4:24), called also Jemuel (Gen. 46:10).

people.name: Jeshua
people.summary: Head of the ninth priestly order (Ezra 2:36); called also Jeshuah (1 Chr. 24:11).

people.name: Jether
people.summary: The father of Amasa, David’s general (1 Kings 2:5, 32); called Ithra (2 Sam. 17:25).

people.name: Jeush
people.summary: The oldest of Esau’s three sons by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:5, 14, 18).

people.name: Jezaniah
people.summary: A Maachathite (2 Kings 25:23; Jer. 40:8; 42:1).

people.name: Jezreel
people.summary: Respond.

people.name: Jobab
people.summary: King of Edom, succeeded Bela (Gen. 36:33, 34).

people.name: Joel
people.summary: The oldest of Samuel’s two sons appointed by him as judges in Beersheba (1 Sam. 8:2).

people.name: Joiarib
people.summary: The founder of one of the courses of the priests (Neh. 11:10).

people.name: Jonas
people.summary: The father of the apostles Peter (John 21:15-17) and Andrew; but the reading should be (also in 1:42), as in the Revised Version, “John,” instead of Jonas.

people.name: Josiah
people.summary: Common in later times among the Jews in Palestine (Matt. 23:37; Luke 13:34).

people.name: Jotham
people.summary: The youngest of Gideon’s seventy sons. He escaped when the rest were put to death by the order of Abimelech (Judg. 9:5). When “the citizens of Shechem and the whole house of Millo” were gathered together “by the plain of the pillar” (i.e., the stone set up by Joshua, 24:26; comp. Gen. 35:4) “that was in Shechem, to make Abimelech king,” from one of the heights of Mount Gerizim he protested against their doing so in the earliest parable, that of the bramble-king.

people.name: Keturah
people.summary: Incense, the wife of Abraham, whom he married probably after Sarah’s death (Gen. 25:1-6), by whom he had six sons, whom he sent away into the east country.

people.name: Korah
people.summary: The third son of Esau, by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:14; 1 Chr. 1:35).

people.name: Lamech
people.summary: The fifth in descent from Cain. He was the first to violate the primeval ordinance of marriage (Gen. 4:18-24). His address to his two wives, Adah and Zillah (4:23, 24), is the only extant example of antediluvian poetry.

people.name: Lazarus
people.summary: Jesus restores him to life four days after his death, lives in the town of Bethany near Jerusalem, He is identified as the brother of the sisters Mary and Martha.

people.name: Lydia
people.summary: A woman of Thyatira, a “seller of purple,” who dwelt in Philippi (Acts 16:14, 15). She was not a Jewess but a proselyte. The Lord opened her heart as she heard the gospel from the lips of Paul (16:13).

people.name: Mahlah
people.summary: Disease, one of the five daughters of Zelophehad (Num. 27:1-11) who had their father’s inheritance, the law of inheritance having been altered in their favour.

people.name: Mahlon
people.summary: Sickly, the elder of Elimelech the Bethlehemite’s two sons by Naomi.

people.name: Malchi-shua
people.summary: King of help, one of the four sons of Saul (1 Chr. 8:33).

people.name: Merab
people.summary: Increase, the eldest of Saul’s two daughters (1 Sam. 14:49). She was betrothed to David after his victory over Goliath, but does not seem to have entered heartily into this arrangement (18:2, 17, 19).

people.name: Milcah
people.summary: Belonged to clans of Menasseh.

people.name: Mizraim
people.summary: The dual form of matzor, meaning a “mound” or “fortress,” the name of a people descended from Ham (Gen. 10:6, 13; 1 Chr. 1:8, 11). It was the name generally given by the Hebrews to the land of Egypt, and may denote the two Egypts, the Upper and the Lower.

people.name: Moza
people.summary: The son of Zimri, of the posterity of Saul (1 Chr. 8:36, 37; 9:42, 43).

people.name: Nadab
people.summary: The son and successor of Jeroboam, the king of Israel (1 Kings 14:20). While engaged with all Israel in laying siege to Gibbethon, a town of southern Dan (Josh. 19:44), a conspiracy broke out in his army, and he was slain by Baasha (1 Kings 15:25-28), after a reign of two years (B.C. 955-953).

people.name: Nimrod
people.summary: Firm, a descendant of Cush, the son of Ham. He was the first who claimed to be a “mighty one in the earth.” Babel was the beginning of his kingdom, which he gradually enlarged (Gen. 10:8-10).

people.name: Noah
people.summary: Rest, (Heb. Noah) the grandson of Methuselah (Gen. 5:25-29), who was for two hundred and fifty years contemporary with Adam, and the son of Lamech, who was about fifty years old at the time of Adam’s death.

people.name: Oreb
people.summary: Raven, a prince of Midian, who, being defeated by Gideon and put to straits, was slain along with Zeeb (Judg. 7:20-25).

people.name: Pahath-moab
people.summary: Governor of Moab, a person whose descendants returned from the Captivity and assisted in rebuilding Jerusalem (Ezra 2:6; 8:4; 10:30).

people.name: Pashur
people.summary: In charge of temple.

people.name: Pharaoh
people.summary: The Pharaoh who was on the throne when Abram went down into Egypt (Gen. 12:10-20) was probably one of the Hyksos, or “shepherd kings.” The Egyptians called the nomad tribes of Syria Shasu, “plunderers,” their king or chief Hyk, and hence the name of those invaders who conquered the native kings and established a strong government, with Zoan or Tanis as their capital.

people.name: Rechab
people.summary: One of Ishbosheth’s “captains of bands” or leaders of predatory troops (2 Sam. 4:2).

people.name: Rehum
people.summary: The “chancellor” of Artaxerxes, who sought to stir him up against the Jews (Ezra 4:8-24) and prevent the rebuilding of the walls and the temple of Jerusalem.

people.name: Rizpah
people.summary: Coal; hot stone, the daughter of Aiah, and one of Saul’s concubines.

people.name: Seir
people.summary: A Horite; one of the “dukes” of Edom (Gen. 36:20-30).

people.name: Seraiah
people.summary: A priest of the days of Jehoiakim (Neh. 12:1, 12).

people.name: Shallum
people.summary: The son of Jabesh, otherwise unknown. He “conspired against Zachariah, and smote him before the people, and slew him, and reigned in his stead” (2 Kings 15:10).

people.name: Shaphat
people.summary: The father of Elisha (1 Kings 19:16-19).

people.name: Shaul
people.summary: A king of Edom (Gen. 36:37, 38); called Shaul in 1 Chr. 1:48.

people.name: Shaul
people.summary: Son of Simeon.

people.name: Shavsha
people.summary: (“Seraiah,” 2 Sam. 8:17; “Shisha,” 1 Kings 4:3), one of David’s secretaries (1 Chr. 18:16).

people.name: Shethar-boznai
people.summary: Star of splendour, a Persian officer who vainly attempted to hinder the rebuilding of the temple (Ezra 5:3, 6; 6:6, 13).

people.name: Shimshai
people.summary: The shining one, or sunny, the secretary of Rehum the chancellor, who took part in opposing the rebuilding of the temple after the Captivity (Ezra 4:8, 9, 17-23).

people.name: Shobach
people.summary: Poured out, the “captain of the host of Hadarezer” when he mustered his vassals and tributaries from beyond “the river Euphrates” (2 Sam. 10:15-18); called also Shophach (1 Chr. 19:16).

people.name: Shobal
people.summary: One of the sons of Caleb, and a descendant of Hur (1 Chr. 2:50, 52; 4:1, 2).

people.name: Simon
people.summary: One of the twelve apostles, called the Canaanite (Matt. 10:4; Mark 3:18). This word “Canaanite” does not mean a native of Canaan, but is derived from the Syriac word Kanean or Kaneniah, which was the name of a Jewish sect.

people.name: Simon
people.summary: A sorcerer of great repute for his magical arts among the Samaritans (Acts 8:9-11). He afterwards became a professed convert to the faith under the preaching of Philip the deacon and evangelist (12, 13).

people.name: Simon
people.summary: A Christian at Joppa, a tanner by trade, with whom Peter on one occasion lodged (Acts 9:43).

people.name: Tatnai
people.summary: Gift, a Persian governor (Heb. pehah, i.e., “satrap;” modern “pasha”) “on this side the river”, i.e., of the whole tract on the west of the Euphrates.

people.name: Togarmah
people.summary: A son of Gomer, and grandson of Japheth (Gen. 10:3).

people.name: Toi
people.summary: A king of Hamath, who sent “Joram his son unto King David to salute him,” when he “heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadadezer” (2 Sam. 8:9, 10).

people.name: Tola
people.summary: Eldest son of Issachar (Gen. 46:13).

people.name: Uzzi
people.summary: The son of Bukki, and a descendant of Aaron (1 Chr. 6:5, 51; Ezra 7:4).

people.name: Zabdi
people.summary: An ancestor of Achan (Josh. 7:1, 17, 18).

people.name: Zadok
people.summary: The Priest.

people.name: Zerah
people.summary: One of the sons of Simeon (Gen. 46:10; Ex. 6:15).

people.name: Zophar
people.summary: Chirping, one of Job’s friends who came to condole with him in his distress (Job 2:11. The LXX. render here “king of the Mineans” = Ma’in, Maonites, Judg. 10:12, in Southern Arabia).

people.name: Abiezer
people.summary: One of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:27; comp. 1 Chr. 27:12).

people.name: Abigail
people.summary: The sister of David, and wife of Jether an Ishmaelite (1 Chr. 2:16, 17).

people.name: Abinadab
people.summary: The second of the eight sons of Jesse (1 Sam. 16:8).

people.name: Achbor
people.summary: An Edomitish king (Gen. 36:38; 1 Chr. 1:49).

people.name: Achbor
people.summary: The son of Micah, one of those whom Josiah sent to the prophetess Huldah to ascertain from her the meaning of the recently discovered book of the law (2 Chr. 34:20).

people.name: Adah
people.summary: The first of Lamech’s two wives, and the mother of Jabal and Jubal (Gen. 4:19, 20, 23).

people.name: Adin
people.summary: Ezra 8:6.

people.name: Adonikam
people.summary: Whom the Lord sets up, one of those “which came with Zerubbabel” (Ezra 2:13).

people.name: Ahiman
people.summary: One of the three giant Anakim brothers whom Caleb and the spies saw in Mount Hebron (Num. 13:22) when they went in to explore the land.

people.name: Ahio
people.summary: One of the sons of Abinadab the Levite.

people.name: Amaziah
people.summary: A priest of the golden calves at Bethel (Amos 7:10-17).

people.name: Ammiel
people.summary: The father of Machir of Lo-debar, in whose house Mephibosheth resided (2 Sam. 9:4, 5; 17:27).

people.name: Anah
people.summary: Wife of Esau.

people.name: Ananias
people.summary: One of the members of the church at Jerusalem, who conspired with his wife Sapphira to deceive the brethren, and who fell down and immediately expired after he had uttered the falsehood (Acts 5:5).

people.name: Arad
people.summary: One of the sons of Beriah (1 Chr. 8:15).

people.name: Aram
people.summary: The son of Shem (Gen. 10:22); according to Gen. 22:21, a grandson of Nahor.

people.name: Artaxerxes
people.summary: The king who obstructed the rebuilding of the temple (Ezra 4:7).

people.name: Asahiah
people.summary: The son of Amoz (Isa. 1:1; 2:1), who was apparently a man of humble rank. His wife was called “the prophetess” (8:3), either because she was endowed with the prophetic gift, like Deborah (Judg. 4:4) and Huldah (2 Kings 22:14-20), or simply because she was the wife of “the prophet” (Isa. 38:1).

people.name: Asaph
people.summary: The “recorder” in the time of Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:18, 37).

people.name: Asenath
people.summary: An Egyptian name, meaning “gift of the sun-god”, daughter of Potipherah, priest of On or Heliopolis, wife of Joseph (Gen. 41:45).

people.name: Ashkenaz
people.summary: One of the three sons of Gomer (Gen. 10:3), and founder of one of the tribes of the Japhetic race.

people.name: Ashtoreth
people.summary: The moon goddess of the Phoenicians, representing the passive principle in nature, their principal female deity; frequently associated with the name of Baal, the sun-god, their chief male deity (Judg. 10:6; 1 Sam. 7:4; 12:10).

people.name: Augustus
people.summary: The cognomen of the first Roman emperor, C. Julius Caesar Octavianus, during whose reign Christ was born (Luke 2:1). His decree that “all the world should be taxed” was the divinely ordered occasion of Jesus’ being born, according to prophecy (Micah 5:2), in Bethlehem.

people.name: Azariah
people.summary: Johanan the father.

people.name: Azariah
people.summary: Nehemiah.

people.name: Bani
people.summary: One of David's thirty-seven warriors.

people.name: Bani
people.summary: Sherebiah.

people.name: Bebai
people.summary: The descendants of Bebai.

people.name: Ben-hadad
people.summary: Son of the preceding, also king of Syria. He was long engaged in war against Israel.

people.name: Berechiah
people.summary: Son of Shimea, and father of Asaph the musician (1 Chr. 6:39; 15:17).

people.name: Berechiah
people.summary: The father of Meshullam the builder.

people.name: Bernice
people.summary: Bearer of victory, the eldest daughter of Agrippa I., the Herod Agrippa of Acts 12:20. After the early death of her first husband she was married to her uncle Herod, king of Chalcis.

people.name: Bigvai
people.summary: Head of Jewish family.

people.name: Bilgah
people.summary: A priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:5, 18).

people.name: Bukki
people.summary: The son of Abishua.

people.name: Carmi
people.summary: The son of Zimri, and the father of Achan (Josh. 7:1), “the troubler of Israel.”

people.name: Chilion
people.summary: The pining one, the younger son of Elimelech and Naomi, and husband of Orpah, Ruth’s sister (Ruth 1:2; 4:9).

people.name: Demas
people.summary: A companion and fellow-labourer of Paul during his first imprisonment at Rome (Philemon 1:24; Col. 4:14).

people.name: Demetrius
people.summary: A silversmith at Ephesus, whose chief occupation was to make “silver shrines for Diana”, Acts 19:24, i.e., models either of the temple of Diana or of the statue of the goddess.

people.name: Dodo
people.summary: An Ahohite, father of Eleazar, who was one of David’s three heroes (2 Sam. 23:9; 1 Chr. 11:12).

people.name: Dorcas
people.summary: (in Greek called Dorcas), gazelle, a disciple at Joppa. She was distinguished for her alms-deeds and good works. Peter, who was sent for from Lydda on the occasion of her death, prayed over the dead body, and said, “Tabitha, arise.”

people.name: Eleasah
people.summary: A descendant of king Saul (1 Chr. 8:37; 9:43).

people.name: Eleazar
people.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 23:21, 22).

people.name: Eliab
people.summary: Lyre player.

people.name: Eliada
people.summary: One of David’s sons born after his establishment in Jerusalem (2 Sam. 5:16).

people.name: Eliashib
people.summary: Son of Zabbai.

people.name: Elihu
people.summary: The son of Tohu, and grandfather of Elkanah (1 Sam. 1:1).

people.name: Eliphalet
people.summary: God his deliverance, one of David’s sons (2 Sam. 5:16); called also Eliphelet (1 Chr. 3:8).

people.name: Elishua
people.summary: God his salvation, a son of David, 2 Sam. 5:15 = Elishama, 1 Chr. 3:6.

people.name: Elnathan
people.summary: Sent to find Uriah.

people.name: Epaphras
people.summary: Lovely, spoken of by Paul (Col. 1:7; 4:12) as “his dear fellow-servant,” and “a faithful minister of Christ.” He was thus evidently with him at Rome when he wrote to the Colossians.

people.name: Ephah
people.summary: Descendant of Keturah.

people.name: Erastus
people.summary: A companion of Paul at Ephesus, who was sent by him along with Timothy into Macedonia (Acts 19:22).

people.name: Ezra
people.summary: A priest among those that returned to Jerusalem under Zerubabel (Neh. 12:1).

people.name: Gallio
people.summary: The elder brother of Seneca the philosopher, who was tutor and for some time minister of the emperor Nero. He was “deputy”, i.e., proconsul, as in Revised Version, of Achaia, under the emperor Claudius, when Paul visited Corinth (Acts 18:12).

people.name: Gareb
people.summary: One of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:38), an Ithrite.

people.name: Gera
people.summary: The father of Ehud the judge (Judg. 3:15).

people.name: Guni
people.summary: Son of Naphtali.

people.name: Hadad
people.summary: One of the Edomitish kings (Gen. 36:39) about the time of Saul.

people.name: Hamul
people.summary: Spared, one of the sons of Pharez, son of Judah (1 Chr. 2:5).

people.name: Hamutal
people.summary: Kinsman of the dew, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, wife of king Josiah, and mother of king Jehoahaz (2 Kings 23:31), also of king Zedekiah (2 Kings 24:18).

people.name: Hegai
people.summary: Eunuch, had charge of the harem of Ahasuerus (Esther 2:8).

people.name: Heleb
people.summary: Fatness, one of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:29).

people.name: Helez
people.summary: One of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:26).

people.name: Hodijah
people.summary: One of the Levites who assisted Ezra in expounding the law (Neh. 8:7; 9:5).

people.name: Hosea
people.summary: Salvation, the son of Beeri, and author of the book of prophecies bearing his name. He belonged to the kingdom of Israel. “His Israelitish origin is attested by the peculiar, rough, Aramaizing diction, pointing to the northern part of Palestine; by the intimate acquaintance he evinces with the localities of Ephraim (5:1; 6:8, 9; 12:12; 14:6, etc.); by passages like 1:2, where the kingdom is styled ‘the land’, and 7:5, where the Israelitish king is designated as ‘our’ king.”

people.name: Huram
people.summary: Generally “Huram,” one of the sons of Bela (1 Chr. 8:5).

people.name: Ibhar
people.summary: Chosen, one of David’s sons (1 Chr. 3:6; 2 Sam. 5:15).

people.name: Iddo
people.summary: Lovely. A prophet of Judah who wrote the history of Rehoboam and Abijah (2 Chr. 12:15).

people.name: Imnah
people.summary: The first-born of Asher.

people.name: Ira
people.summary: A Tekoite, one of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:26).

people.name: Jabesh
people.summary: The father of Shallum (2 Kings 15:10, 13, 14), who usurped the throne of Israel on the death of Zachariah.

people.name: Jahzeel
people.summary: Allotted by God, the first of the sons of Naphtali (Gen. 46:24).

people.name: Japhia
people.summary: One of the sons of David (2 Sam. 5:15), born in Jerusalem.

people.name: Jashub
people.summary: The third of Issachar’s four sons (1 Chr. 7:1); called also Job (Gen. 46:13).

people.name: Jedaiah
people.summary: Knowing Jehovah.

people.name: Jediael
people.summary: One of the sons of Benjamin, whose descendants numbered 17,200 warriors (1 Chr. 7:6, 10, 11).

people.name: Jehiel
people.summary: One of the Levites “of the second degree,” appointed to conduct the music on the occasion of the ark’s being removed to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

people.name: Jehudi
people.summary: A Jew, son of Nethaniah.

people.name: Jeremiah
people.summary: The father of Hamutal (2 Kings 23:31), the wife of Josiah.

people.name: Jeroham
people.summary: Father of Elkanah, and grandfather of the prophet Samuel (1 Sam. 1:1).

people.name: Johanan
people.summary: A priest.

people.name: Joiakim
people.summary: (whom Jehovah has set up) = Jehoiakim, a high priest, the son and successor of Jeshua (Neh. 12:10, 12, 26).

people.name: Jokshan
people.summary: Snarer, the second son of Abraham and Keturah (Gen. 25:2, 3; 1 Chr. 1:32).

people.name: Judas
people.summary: A Christian teacher, surnamed Barsabas. He was sent from Jerusalem to Antioch along with Paul and Barnabas with the decision of the council (Acts 15:22, 27, 32).

people.name: Jude
people.summary: Judas. Among the apostles there were two who bore this name, (1) Judas (Jude 1:1; Matt. 13:55; John 14:22; Acts 1:13), called also Lebbaeus or Thaddaeus (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18); and (2) Judas Iscariot (Matt. 10:4; Mark 3:19).

people.name: Kenaz
people.summary: The sons of Eliphaz.

people.name: Kish
people.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 23:21; 24:29).

people.name: Kore
people.summary: A Levite and temple-warder of the Korahites, the son of Asaph.

people.name: Luke
people.summary: The evangelist, was a Gentile. The date and circumstances of his conversion are unknown. According to his own statement (Luke 1:2), he was not an “eye-witness and minister of the word from the beginning.”

people.name: Maaseiah
people.summary: The father of the priest Zephaniah (Jer. 21:1; 37:3).

people.name: Machir
people.summary: A descendant of the preceding, residing at Lo-debar, where he maintained Jonathan’s son Mephibosheth till he was taken under the care of David (2 Sam. 9:4), and where he afterwards gave shelter to David himself when he was a fugitive (17:27).

people.name: Mahli
people.summary: Bon of Mushi and grandson of Merari.

people.name: Malluch
people.summary: A priest who returned from Babylon (Neh. 12:2).

people.name: Mamre
people.summary: An Amoritish chief in alliance with Abraham (Gen. 14:13, 24).

people.name: Memucan
people.summary: Dignified, one of the royal counsellors at the court of Ahasuerus, by whose suggestion Vashti was divorced (Esther 1:14, 16, 21).

people.name: Meshullam
people.summary: Nehemiah 8:4.

people.name: Michah
people.summary: The first in rank of the priests of the family of Kohathites (1 Chr. 23:20).

people.name: Mikloth
people.summary: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:32; 9:37, 38).

people.name: Miniamin
people.summary: A chief priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:5), called Mijamin (10:7) and Miniamin (12:17).

people.name: Moadiah
people.summary: A priest (Neh. 10:8).

people.name: Mother of the Wife of Simon
Naamah
people.summary: The daughter of the king of Ammon, one of the wives of Solomon, the only one who appears to have borne him a son, viz., Rehoboam (1 Kings 14:21, 31).

people.name: Nahash
people.summary: King of the Ammonites in the time of Saul. The inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead having been exposed to great danger from Nahash, sent messengers to Gibeah to inform Saul of their extremity.

people.name: Nahash
people.summary: Fother of hanun.

people.name: Nahath
people.summary: One of the four sons of Reuel, the son of Esau (Gen. 36:13, 17).

people.name: Nahath
people.summary: A Kohathite Levite (1 Chr. 6:26).

people.name: Nepheg
people.summary: Weak.

people.name: Obadiah
people.summary: A Levite, after the Captivity (1 Chr. 9:16).

people.name: Omar
people.summary: Eloquent, the son of Eliphaz, who was Esau’s eldest son (Gen. 36:11-15).

people.name: Parosh
people.summary: Ramiah.

people.name: Pekahiah
people.summary: The Lord opened his eyes, the son and successor of Menahem on the throne of Israel. He was murdered in the royal palace of Samaria by Pekah, one of the captains of his army (2 Kings 15:23-26), after a reign of two years (B.C. 761-759).

people.name: Phichol
people.summary: Great, the chief captain of the army of Abimelech, the Philistine king of Gerar.

people.name: Philip
people.summary: Mentioned only in connection with the imprisonment of John the Baptist (Matt. 14:3; Mark 6:17; Luke 3:19). He was the son of Herod the Great, and the first husband of Herodias, and the father of Salome.

people.name: Phut
people.summary: One of the sons of Ham (Gen. 10:6).

people.name: Puah
people.summary: The sons of Issachar.

people.name: Rehabiah
people.summary: Enlargement of the Lord, the son of Eliezer, and grandson of Moses (1 Chr. 23:17; 24:21).

people.name: Rimmon
people.summary: A man of Beeroth (2 Sam. 4:2), one of the four Gibeonite cities.

people.name: Serah
people.summary: Abundance; princess, the daughter of Asher and grand-daughter of Jacob (Gen. 46:17); called also Sarah (Num. 26:46; R.V., “Serah”).

people.name: Shalmaneser
people.summary: An Assyrian king (Hos. 10:14), identified with Shalmaneser II. (Sayce) or IV. (Lenormant), the successor of Pul on the throne of Assyria (B.C. 728).

people.name: Shammah
people.summary: One of the “dukes” of Edom (Gen. 36:13, 17).

people.name: Shammua
people.summary: One of David’s sons by Bathsheba (1 Chr. 3:5); called also Shammua (14:4).

people.name: Shebaniah
people.summary: Another Levite (Neh. 9:4, 5).

people.name: Shebaniah
people.summary: A priest who returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:3; marg., or Shebaniah).

people.name: Shelomith
people.summary: Son of Zichri.

people.name: Shemaiah
people.summary: The eldest son of Obed-edom (1 Chr. 26:4-8).

people.name: Shemaiah
people.summary: A false prophet who opposed Jeremiah (Jer. 29:24-32).

people.name: Shemiramoth
people.summary: A Levite in David’s time (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

people.name: Shephatiah
people.summary: Ezra 2:4.

people.name: Shimron
people.summary: Watchman, the fourth son of Issachar (Gen. 46:13; 1 Chr. 7:1; R.V., correctly, “Shimron”).

people.name: Shobab
people.summary: One of David’s sons by Bathseheba (2 Sam. 5:14).

people.name: Shuah
people.summary: A Canaanite whose daughter was married to Judah (1 Chr. 2:3).

people.name: Shubael
people.summary: One of the descendants of Gershom, who had charge of the temple treasures in the time of David (1 Chr. 23:16; 26:24).

people.name: Shuthelah
people.summary: Son of Ephraim.

people.name: Simon
people.summary: A Jew of Cyrene, in North Africa, then a province of Libya. A hundred thousand Jews from Palestine had been settled in this province by Ptolemy Soter (B.C. 323-285), where by this time they had greatly increased in number.

people.name: Stephanas
people.summary: Crown, a member of the church at Corinth, whose family were among those the apostle had baptized (1 Cor. 1:16; 16:15, 17). He has been supposed by some to have been the “jailer of Philippi” (comp. Acts 16:33).

people.name: Talmai
people.summary: One of the Anakim of Hebron, who were slain by the men of Judah under Caleb (Num. 13:22; Josh. 15:14; Judg. 1:10).

people.name: Talmai
people.summary: A king of Geshur, to whom Absalom fled after he had put Amnon to death (2 Sam. 3:3; 13:37).

people.name: Teman
people.summary: Son of Eliphaz.

people.name: Timna
people.summary: Lotan's sister.

people.name: Trophimus
people.summary: A foster-child, an Ephesian who accompanied Paul during a part of his third missionary journey (Acts 20:4; 21:29). He was with Paul in Jerusalem, and the Jews, supposing that the apostle had brought him with him into the temple, raised a tumult which resulted in Paul’s imprisonment.

people.name: Urijah
people.summary: The father of Meremoth, mentioned in Ezra 8:33.

people.name: Urijah
people.summary: A prophet of Kirjath-jearim in the reign of Jehoiakim, king of Judah (Jer. 26:20-23).

people.name: Wife of Simon
people.mother: Mother of the Wife of Simon

people.name: Zacchaeus
people.summary: Pure, a superintendant of customs; a chief tax-gather (publicanus) at Jericho (Luke 19:1-10). “The collection of customs at Jericho, which at this time produced and exported a considerable quantity of balsam, was undoubtedly an important post, and would account for Zacchaeus being a rich man.”

people.name: Zaccur
people.summary: A son of Asaph, and chief of one of the courses of singers as arranged by David (1 Chr. 25:2, 10).

people.name: Zachariah
people.summary: Son of Jeroboam II., king of Israel. On the death of his father there was an interregnum of ten years, at the end of which he succeeded to the throne, which he occupied only six months, having been put to death by Shallum, who usurped the throne.

people.name: Zacharias
people.summary: The son or grandson of Jehoiada, the high priest in the times of Ahaziah and Joash. After the death of Jehoiada he boldly condemned both the king and the people for their rebellion against God (2 Chr. 24:20), which so stirred up their resentment against him that at the king’s commandment they stoned him with stones, and he died “in the court of the house of the Lord” (24:21).

people.name: Zattu
people.summary: Id., one whose descendants returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:8; Neh. 7:13); probably the same as Zatthu.

people.name: Zeeb
people.summary: The wolf, one of the two leaders of the great Midianite host which invaded Israel and was utterly routed by Gideon.

people.name: Zerah
people.summary: Grandson of Esau’s wife Basemath.

people.name: Zeresh
people.summary: Star of Venus, the wife of Haman, whom she instigated to prepare a gallows for Mordecai (Esther 5:10).

people.name: Zillah
people.summary: Shadow, one of the wives of Lamech, of the line of Cain, and mother of Tubal-cain (Gen. 4:19, 22).

people.name: Zipporah
people.summary: A female bird. Reuel’s daughter, who became the wife of Moses (Ex. 2:21).

people.name: Zuph
people.summary: Honeycomb, a Kohathite Levite, ancestor of Elkanah and Samuel (1 Sam. 1:1); called also Zophai (1 Chr. 6:26).

people.name: Abdon
people.summary: The son of Hillel, a Pirathonite, the tenth judge of Israel (Judg. 12:13-15).

people.name: Abdon
people.summary: The first-born of Gibeon of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:30; 9:36).

people.name: Abiah
people.summary: The second son of Samuel (1 Sam. 8:2; 1 Chr. 6:28).

people.name: Abida
people.summary: Or Abi’dah, father of knowledge; knowing, one of the five sons of Midian, who was the son of Abraham by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:33), and apparently the chief of an Arab tribe.

people.name: Abihail
people.summary: The father of Esther and uncle of Mordecai (Esther 2:15).

people.name: Abijah
people.summary: The daughter of Zechariah (2 Chr. 29:1; comp. Isa. 8:2), and afterwards the wife of Ahaz.

people.name: Abijah
people.summary: A descendant of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, a chief of one of the twenty-four orders into which the priesthood was divided by David (1 Chr. 24:10).

people.name: Abimael
people.summary: Father of Mael, one of the sons or descendants of Joktan, in Northern Arabia (Gen. 10:28; 1 Chr. 1:22).

people.name: Abishur
people.summary: Father of the wall; i.e., “mason”, one of the two sons of Shammai of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 2:28, 29).

people.name: Abital
people.summary: Father of dew; i.e., “fresh”, David’s fifth wife (2 Sam. 3:4).

people.name: Adaiah
people.summary: Priest resettling Jerusalem.

people.name: Adaiah
people.summary: Timely (1 Chr. 6:21).

people.name: Adbeel
people.summary: Miracle of God, the third of the twelve sons of Ishmael, and head of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:13; 1 Chr. 1:29).

people.name: Adrammelech
people.summary: A son of Sennacherib, king of Assyria (2 Kings 19:37; Isa. 37:38).

people.name: Adriel
people.summary: Flock of God, the son of Barzillai, the Meholathite, to whom Saul gave in marriage his daughter Merab (1 Sam. 18:19). The five sons that sprang from this union were put to death by the Gibeonites (2 Sam. 21:8, 9.

people.name: Agabus
people.summary: A “prophet,” probably one of the seventy disciples of Christ. He prophesied at Antioch of an approaching famine (Acts 11:27, 28).

people.name: Ahab
people.summary: A false prophet referred to by Jeremiah (Jer. 29:21), of whom nothing further is known.

people.name: Ahiam
people.summary: Mother’s brother, one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:33; 1 Chr. 11:35).

people.name: Ahio
people.summary: One of the sons of Jehiel the Gibeonite (1 Chr. 8:31; 9:37).

people.name: Aholibamah
people.summary: Edomite chief.

people.name: Akan
people.summary: He twists, one of the sons of Ezer, the son of Seir the Horite (1 Chr. 1:42).

people.name: Alemeth
people.summary: One of the sons of Jehoadah, or Jarah, son of Ahaz (1 Chr. 8:36).

people.name: Alexander
people.summary: A coppersmith who, with Hymenaeus and others, promulgated certain heresies regarding the resurrection (1 Tim. 1:19; 2 Tim. 4:14), and made shipwreck of faith and of a good conscience.

people.name: Allon
people.summary: The son of Jedaiah, of the family of the Simeonites, who expelled the Hamites from the valley of Gedor (1 Chr. 4:37).

people.name: Almodad
people.summary: Immeasurable, the first named of the sons of Joktan (Gen. 10:26), the founder of an Arabian tribe.

people.name: Amariah
people.summary: One of the descendants of Aaron by Eleazar (1 Chr. 6:7, 52).

people.name: Amariah
people.summary: A Levite, son of Hebron, of the lineage of Moses (1 Chr. 23:19; 24:23).

people.name: Amasai
people.summary: A Levite, son of Elkanah, of the ancestry of Samuel (1 Chr. 6:25, 35).

people.name: Amittai
people.summary: True, the father of Jonah the prophet, a native of Gath-hepher (2 Kings 14:25; Jonah 1:1).

people.name: Amminadab
people.summary: Chief of the 112 descendants of Uzziel the Levite (1 Chr. 15:10, 11).

people.name: Amon
people.summary: The governor of Samaria in the time of Ahab.

people.name: Amraphel
people.summary: King of Shinar, southern Chaldea, one of the confederates of Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, in a war against Sodom and cities of the plain (Gen. 14:1, 4).

people.name: Anah
people.summary: Discoverer of Hot Springs.

people.name: Anamim
people.summary: The name of an Egyptian tribe descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:13; 1 Chr. 1:11).

people.name: Ananias
people.summary: The high priest before whom Paul was brought in the procuratorship of Felix (Acts 23:2, 5, 24). He was so enraged at Paul’s noble declaration, “I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day,” that he commanded one of his attendants to smite him on the mouth.

people.name: Anath
people.summary: An answer; i.e., to “prayer”, the father of Shamgar, who was one of the judges of Israel (Judg. 3:31).

people.name: Aner
people.summary: A Canaanitish chief who joined his forces with those of Abraham in pursuit of Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:13, 24).

people.name: Arah
people.summary: 652 children.

people.name: Aran
people.summary: Wild goat, a descendant of Seir the Horite (Gen. 36:28).

people.name: Archippus
people.summary: Master of the horse, a “fellow-soldier” of Paul’s (Philemon 1:2), whom he exhorts to renewed activity (Col. 4:17).

people.name: Arioch
people.summary: A king of Ellasar who was confederate with Chedorlamer (Gen. 14:1, 9). The tablets recently discovered by Mr. Pinches (see CHALDEA) show the true reading is Eri-Aku of Larsa.

people.name: Arkite
people.summary: (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15), a designation of certain descendants from the Phoenicians or Sidonians, the inhabitants of Arka, 12 miles north of Tripoli, opposite the northern extremity of Lebanon.

people.name: Asaph
people.summary: Son of Mika.

people.name: Assir
people.summary: Korah.

people.name: Ater
people.summary: Ezra 2:16.

people.name: Ater
people.summary: Ezra 2:42.

people.name: Attai
people.summary: Servant of jarha and his wife.

people.name: Azareel
people.summary: A priest (1 Chr. 9:12).

people.name: Azariah
people.summary: Son of Zadok—the priest.

people.name: Azariah
people.summary: Jehu.

people.name: Azariah
people.summary: High priest in the reign of Uzziah, king of Judah (2 Kings 14:21; 2 Chr. 26:17-20).

people.name: Azariah
people.summary: The chief priest.

people.name: Azmaveth
people.summary: One of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:31).

people.name: Azrikam
people.summary: Father of Hasshub.

people.name: Azubah
people.summary: The daughter of Shilhi, and mother of king Jehoshaphat (1 Kings 22:42).

people.name: Azubah
people.summary: The wife of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:18, 19).

people.name: Baal
people.summary: A Benjamite, son of Jehiel, the progenitor of the Gibeonites (1 Chr. 8:30; 9:36).

people.name: Baanah
people.summary: The father of Heled, who was one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:29; 1 Chr. 11:30).

people.name: Baanah
people.summary: Father of Iteleb, one of David's mighty men.

people.name: Baladan
people.summary: He has given a son, the father of the Babylonian king (2 Kings 20:12; Isa. 39:1) Merodach-baladan.

people.name: Barachel
people.summary: Whom God has blessed, a Buzite, the father of Elihu, one of Job’s friends (Job 32:2, 6).

people.name: Barkos
people.summary: Painter, (Ezra 2:53; Neh. 7:55).

people.name: Barzillai
people.summary: A priest who married a daughter of the preceding (Ezra 2:61).

people.name: Ben-ammi
people.summary: Son of my kindred; i.e., “born of incest”, the son of Lot by his youngest daughter (Gen. 19:38).

people.name: Benaiah
people.summary: Father of Pelatiah.

people.name: Beor
people.summary: The father of Bela, one of the kings of Edom (Gen. 36:32).

people.name: Beriah
people.summary: A Benjamite who with his brother Shema founded Ajalon and expelled the Gittites (1 Chr. 8:13).

people.name: Beriah
people.summary: Son of Shimei.

people.name: Bezai
people.summary: Head of a Jewish family, which returned from Babylon.

people.name: Bigthana
people.summary: One of the eunuchs who “kept the door” in the court of Ahasuerus. With Teresh he conspired against the king’s life.

people.name: Bigvai
people.summary: In my body.

people.name: Bilhan
people.summary: The sons of Ezer.

people.name: Bilshan
people.summary: Son of the tongue; i.e., “eloquent”, a man of some note who returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:2; Neh. 7:7).

people.name: Binnui
people.summary: Son of Henadad.

people.name: Casluhim
people.summary: Fortified, a people descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:14; 1 Chr. 1:12).

people.name: Chenaniah
people.summary: Whom Jehovah hath made.

people.name: Chushan-rishathaim
people.summary: Cush of double wickedness, or governor of two presidencies, the king of Mesopotamia who oppressed Israel in the generation immediately following Joshua (Judg. 3:8).

people.name: Claudius
people.summary: The fourth Roman emperor. He succeeded Caligula (A.D. 41). Though in general he treated the Jews, especially those in Asia and Egypt, with great indulgence, yet about the middle of his reign (A.D. 49) he banished them all from Rome (Acts 18:2).

people.name: Cleophas
people.summary: (abbreviation of Cleopatros), one of the two disciples with whom Jesus conversed on the way to Emmaus on the day of the resurrection (Luke 24:18).

people.name: Crispus
people.summary: Curled, the chief of the synagogue at Corinth (Acts 18:8).

people.name: Daniel
people.summary: David’s second son, “born unto him in Hebron, of Abigail the Carmelitess” (1 Chr. 3:1).

people.name: Daniel
people.summary: David's second son.

people.name: Dedan
people.summary: A son of Raamah (Gen. 10:7). His descendants are mentioned in Isa. 21:13, and Ezek. 27:15.

people.name: Dedan
people.summary: A son of Jokshan, Abraham’s son by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:32). His descendants settled on the Syrian borders about the territory of Edom.

people.name: Delaiah
people.summary: The head of one of the bands of exiles that returned under Zerubbabel to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:60; Neh. 7:62).

people.name: Delaiah
people.summary: A son of Shemaiah, and one of the courtiers to whom Jeremiah’s first roll of prophecy was read (Jer. 36:12).

people.name: Dodanim
people.summary: Leaders, a race descended from Javan (Gen. 10:4). They are known in profane history as the Dardani, originally inhabiting Illyricum. They were a semi-Pelasgic race, and in the ethnographical table (Gen. 10) they are grouped with the Chittim.

people.name: Dodo
people.summary: A Bethlehemite, and father of Elhanan, who was one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:24).

people.name: Ebal
people.summary: A descendant of Seir the Horite (Gen. 36:23).

people.name: Ebal
people.summary: A descendant of Eber (1 Chr. 1:22), called also Obal (Gen. 10:28).

people.name: Eder
people.summary: The second of the three sons of Mushi, of the family of Merari, appointed to the Levitical office (1 Chr. 23:23; 24:30).

people.name: Eglah
people.summary: A heifer, one of David’s wives, and mother of Ithream (2 Sam. 3:5; 1 Chr. 3:3).

people.name: Elah
people.summary: One of the Edomite chiefs or “dukes” of Mount Seir (Gen. 36:41).

people.name: Elam
people.summary: Highland, the son of Shem (Gen. 10:22), and the name of the country inhabited by his descendants (14:1, 9; Isa. 11:11; 21:2, etc.) lying to the east of Babylonia, and extending to the shore of the Mediterranean, a distance in a direct line of about 1,000 miles.

people.name: Eldad
people.summary: Whom God has loved, one of the seventy elders whom Moses appointed (Num. 11:26, 27) to administer justice among the people. He, with Medad, prophesied in the camp instead of going with the rest to the tabernacle, as Moses had commanded.

people.name: Eleasah
people.summary: One of the descendants of Judah, of the family of Hezron (1 Chr. 2:39, “Eleasah”).

people.name: Eleazar
people.summary: The son of Dodo the Ahohite, of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the three most eminent of David’s thirty-seven heroes (1 Chr. 11:12) who broke through the Philistine host and brought him water from the well of Bethlehem (2 Sam. 23:9, 16).

people.name: Elhanan
people.summary: A warrior of the time of David famed for his exploits. In the Authorized Version (2 Sam. 21:19) it is recorded that “Elhanan the son of Jaare-oregim, a Bethlehemite, slew the brother of Goliath.”

people.name: Elhanan
people.summary: The son of Dodo, and one of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:24).

people.name: Eliam
people.summary: The father of Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah (2 Sam. 11:3).

people.name: Eliathah
people.summary: To whom God will come, one of the foureen sons of the Levite Heman, and musician of the temple in the time of David (1 Chr. 25:4).

people.name: Eliel
people.summary: Son of Hebron.

people.name: Elipheleh
people.summary: God will distinguish him, one of the porters appointed to play “on the Sheminith” on the occasion of the bringing up of the ark to the city of David (1 Chr. 15:18, 21).

people.name: Elishah
people.summary: The oldest of the four sons of Javan (Gen. 10:4), whose descendants peopled Greece. It has been supposed that Elishah’s descendants peopled the Peloponnesus, which was known by the name of Elis.

people.name: Elishama
people.summary: One of David’s sons (2 Sam. 5:16).

people.name: Elkanah
people.summary: The second son of Korah (Ex. 6:24), or, according to 1 Chr. 6:22, 23, more correctly his grandson.

people.name: Elkanah
people.summary: Prophet of Levi.

people.name: Elkanah
people.summary: His son.

people.name: Elon
people.summary: A Hittite, father of Bashemath, Esau’s wife (Gen. 26:34).

people.name: Elon
people.summary: One of the sons of Zebulun (Gen. 46:14).

people.name: Elon
people.summary: The eleventh of the Hebrew judges. He held office for ten years (Judg. 12:11, 12).

people.name: Elymas
people.summary: Magician or sorcerer, the Arabic name of the Jew Bar-jesus, who withstood Paul and Barnabas in Cyprus.

people.name: Enoch
people.summary: The eldest son of Cain (Gen. 4:17), who built a city east of Eden in the land of Nod, and called it “after the name of his son Enoch.”

people.name: Epher
people.summary: One of the sons of Midian, who was Abraham’s son by Keturah (Gen. 25:4).

people.name: Eshcol
people.summary: A young Amoritish chief who joined Abraham in the recovery of Lot from the hands of Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:13, 24).

people.name: Ethan
people.summary: A Levite of the family of Gershom (1 Chr. 6:21), probably the same as Ethan (42).

people.name: Evil-merodach
people.summary: Merodach’s man, the son and successor of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon (2 Kings 25:27; Jer. 52:31, 34). He seems to have reigned but two years (B.C. 562-560).

people.name: Ezekiel
people.summary: One of the great prophets, the son of Buzi the priest (Ezek. 1:3). He was one of the Jewish exiles who settled at Tel-Abib, on the banks of the Chebar, “in the land of the Chaldeans.”

people.name: Gahar
people.summary: Lurking-place, one of the chief of the Nethinim, whose descendants returned to Jerusalem under Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:47).

people.name: Gaius
people.summary: A Macedonian, Paul’s fellow-traveller, and his host at Corinth when he wrote his Epistle to the Romans (16:23). He with his household were baptized by Paul (1 Cor. 1:14).

people.name: Galal
people.summary: Son ofJeduthun.

people.name: Gamaliel
people.summary: The son of rabbi Simeon, and grandson of the famous rabbi Hillel. He was a Pharisse, and therefore the opponent of the party of the Sadducees.

people.name: Gedaliah
people.summary: the son of Jeduthum (1 Chr. 25:3, 9).

people.name: Giddel
people.summary: His sons were temple servants.

people.name: Girgasite
people.summary: Dwelling in clayey soil, the descendants of the fifth son of Canaan (Gen. 10:16), one of the original tribes inhabiting the land of Canaan before the time of the Israelites (Gen. 15:21; Deut. 7:1).

people.name: Hadar
people.summary: A son of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15); in 1 Chr. 1:30 written Hadad.

people.name: Hadoram
people.summary: The fifth son of Joktan, the founder of an Arab tribe (Gen. 10:27; 1 Chr. 1:21).

people.name: Hammelech
people.summary: The king’s, the father of Jerahmeel, mentioned in Jer. 36:26. Some take this word as a common noun, “the king”, and understand that Jerahmeel was Jehoiakim’s son.

people.name: Hanan
people.summary: A descendant of Saul (1 Chr. 8:38).

people.name: Hanan
people.summary: One of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:46).

people.name: Hanan
people.summary: One of the Levites who assisted Ezra (Neh. 8:7).

people.name: Hanani
people.summary: One of the sons of Heman (1 Chr. 25:4, 25).

people.name: Hanani
people.summary: Probably a brother of Nehemiah (Neh. 1:2; 7:2), who reported to him the melancholy condition of Jerusalem.

people.name: Hananiah
people.summary: Son of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:19, 21).

people.name: Hananiah
people.summary: One of the sons of Heman (1 Chr. 25:4, 23).

people.name: Harhur
people.summary: Fever, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:51).

people.name: Harsha
people.summary: Worker or enchanter, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:52; Neh. 7:54).

people.name: Hashabiah
people.summary: One of the Levite leaders in the time of Ezra.

people.name: Hashabiah
people.summary: Son of Jeduthun.

people.name: Hasrah
people.summary: Poverty, “keeper of the wardrobe,” i.e., of the sacerdotal vestments (2 Chr. 34:22); called Harhas 2 Kings 22:14.

people.name: Hasshub
people.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari (Neh. 11:15; 1 Chr. 9:14).

people.name: Hasupha
people.summary: Uncovered, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:43; Neh. 7:46).

people.name: Hatipha
people.summary: Captured, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:54).

people.name: Hatita
people.summary: Exploration, one of the temple porters or janitors (Ezra 2:42).

people.name: Hattush
people.summary: A priest who returned with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:2).

people.name: Havilah
people.summary: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

people.name: Havilah
people.summary: A son of Joktan (Gen. 10:29; 1 Chr. 1:23).

people.name: Hazarmaveth
people.summary: Court of death, the third son of Joktan, and a region in Arabia-Felix settled by him (Gen. 10:26; 1 Chr. 1:20).

people.name: Helah
people.summary: Rust, (1 Chr. 4:5, 7), one of the wives of Ashur.

people.name: Helek
people.summary: A portion, (Josh. 17:2), descended from Manasseh.

people.name: Helem
people.summary: Zech. 6:10, one who returned from Babylon.

people.name: Henadad
people.summary: Favour of Hadad, the name of a Levite after the Captivity (Ezra 3:9).

people.name: Hezekiah
people.summary: Babylon.

people.name: Hezrai
people.summary: A Carmelite, one of David’s warriors (1 Chr. 11:37).

people.name: Hillel
people.summary: Praising, a Pirathonite, father of the judge Abdon (Judg. 12:13, 15).

people.name: Hobab
people.summary: Beloved, the Kenite, has been usually identified with Jethro, Ex. 18:5, 27; comp. Num. 10:29, 30.

people.name: Hoshaiah
people.summary: Father ofJezaniah.

people.name: Hotham
people.summary: A stroke, great-grandson of Asher (1 Chr. 7:35).

people.name: Hul
people.summary: Circle, the second son of Aram (Gen. 10:23), and grandson of Shem.

people.name: Huldah
people.summary: Weasel, a prophetess; the wife of Shallum. She was consulted regarding the “book of the law” discovered by the high priest Hilkiah (2 Kings 22:14-20; 2 Chr. 34:22-28).

people.name: Hur
people.summary: One of the five princes of Midian who were defeated and slain by the Israelites under the command of Phinehas (Num. 31:8).

people.name: Hurai
people.summary: Linen-worker, one of David’s heroes, a native of the valley of Mount Gaash (1 Chr. 11:32).

people.name: Hushim
people.summary: Son of Dan.

people.name: Hushim
people.summary: Son of Dan.

people.name: Ibzan
people.summary: Illustrious, the tenth judge of Israel (Judg. 12:8-10).

people.name: Iddo
people.summary: A priest.

people.name: Ilai
people.summary: An Ahohite, one of David’s chief warriors (1 Chr. 11:29); called also Zalmon (2 Sam. 23:28).

people.name: Immer
people.summary: Son of Meshullam.

people.name: Ira
people.summary: An Ithrite, also one of David’s heroes (2 Sam. 23:38).

people.name: Iram
people.summary: Citizen, chief of an Edomite tribe in Mount Seir (Gen. 36:43).

people.name: Ishbak
people.summary: Leaving, one of Abraham’s sons by Keturah (Gen. 25:2).

people.name: Ishmael
people.summary: Ishmael is the figure known in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam as Abraham's son, born to Haga.

people.name: Ittai
people.summary: A Benjamite, one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:29).

people.name: Jaala
people.summary: A wild she-goat, one of the Nethinim, whose descendants returned from the Captivity (Neh. 7:58).

people.name: Jaaziah
people.summary: Comforted by Jehovah, a descendant of Merari the Levite (1 Chr. 24:26, 27).

people.name: Jaaziel
people.summary: Comforted by God, a Levitical musician (1 Chr. 15:18).

people.name: Jabez
people.summary: A descendant of Judah, of whom it is recorded that “God granted him that which he requested” (1 Chr. 4:9, 10).

people.name: Jachin
people.summary: One of the priests who returned from the Exile (1 Chr. 9:10).

people.name: Jaddua
people.summary: The last high priest mentioned in the Old Testament (Neh. 12:11, 22), sons of Jonathan.

people.name: Jahath
people.summary: A son of Shimei, and grandson of Gershom (1 Chr. 23:10).

people.name: Jahaziel
people.summary: The third son of Hebron (1 Chr. 23:19).

people.name: Jair
people.summary: The father of Elhanan, who slew Lahmi, the brother of Goliath (1 Chr. 20:5).

people.name: Jair
people.summary: Gileadite.

people.name: Jairus
people.summary: A ruler of the synagogue at Capernaum, whose only daughter Jesus restored to life (Mark 5:22; Luke 8:41).

people.name: Jasher
people.summary: Upright. “The Book of Jasher,” rendered in the LXX. “the Book of the Upright One,” by the Vulgate “the Book of Just Ones,” was probably a kind of national sacred song-book, a collection of songs in praise of the heroes of Israel, a “book of golden deeds,” a national anthology.

people.name: Jashobeam
people.summary: Dweller among the people; or to whom the people turn, the Hachmonite (1 Chr. 11:11), one of David’s chief heroes who joined him at Ziklag (12:6).

people.name: Jebusite
people.summary: The name of the original inhabitants of Jebus, mentioned frequently among the seven nations doomed to destruction (Gen. 10:16; 15:21; Ex. 3:8, 17; 13:5, etc.).

people.name: Jecoliah
people.summary: Able through Jehovah, the wife of King Amaziah, and mother of King Uzziah (2 Chr. 26:3).

people.name: Jedaiah
people.summary: Invoker of Jehovah.

people.name: Jeduthun
people.summary: The King's Seer.

people.name: Jehoaddan
people.summary: Jehovah his ornament, the wife of King Jehoash, and mother of King Amaziah (2 Kings 14:2).

people.name: Jehoshabeath
people.summary: Jehovah-swearing, the daughter of Jehoram, the king of Israel. She is called Jehoshabeath in 2 Chr. 22:11.

people.name: Jehoshaphat
people.summary: The son of Nimshi, and father of Jehu, king of Israel (2 Kings 9:2, 14).

people.name: Jehozabad
people.summary: The son of Shomer, one of the two conspirators who put king Jehoash to death in Millo in Jerusalem (2 Kings 12:21).

people.name: Jeremoth
people.summary: 1 Chr. 24:30, a Merarite Levite.

people.name: Jerimoth
people.summary: A Levitical musician under Heman his father (1 Chr. 25:4).

people.name: Jeroham

people.name: Lo-ruhamah

people.name: Lucius

people.name: Maacah

people.name: Maachah

people.name: Maaseiah

people.name: Maaseiah

people.name: Maasiai

people.name: Madai

people.name: Mahath

people.name: Maher-shalal-hash-baz
people.summary: Plunder speedeth; spoil hasteth, (Isa. 8:1-3; comp. Zeph. 1:14), a name Isaiah was commanded first to write in large characters on a tablet, and afterwards to give as a symbolical name to a son that was to be born to him (Isa. 8:1, 3), as denoting the sudden attack on Damascus and Syria by the Assyrian army.

people.name: Malcham
people.summary: (2 Sam. 12:30, Heb., R.V., “their king;” Jer. 49:1, 3, R.V.; Zeph. 1:5), the national idol of the Ammonites. When Rabbah was taken by David, the crown of this idol was among the spoils.

people.name: Malchijah
people.summary: The first Malchijah mentioned in the Bible was a priest of ancient Israel after the order of Aaron, during the reign of King David in the 10th century BC. Malchijah led the fifth of the 24 priestly divisions. The biblical passage of 1 Chronicles 24 documents the division of the priests during the reign of King David. These priests were all descendants of Aaron, who had four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. However, Nadab and Abihu died before Aaron and only Eleazar and Ithamar had sons. One priest, Zadok, from Eleazar's descendants and another priest, Ahimelech, from Ithamar's descendants were designated to help create the various priestly orders. Sixteen of Eleazar's descendants were selected to head priestly orders while only eight of Ithamar's descendants were so chosen. The passage states that this was done because of the greater number of leaders among Eleazar's descendants. Lots were drawn to designate the order of ministering for the heads of the priestly orders when they entered the temple. Since each order was responsible for ministering during a different week, Malchijah's order was stationed as a watch at the Tabernacle during the fifth week of the year on the Hebrew calendar.

people.name: Mallothi
people.summary: My fulness, a Kohathite Levite, one of the sons of Heman the Levite (1 Chr. 25:4), and chief of the nineteenth division of the temple musicians (26).

people.name: Mash
people.summary: (= Meshech 1 Chr. 1:17), one of the four sons of Aram, and the name of a tribe descended from him (Gen. 10:23) inhabiting some part probably of Mesopotamia.

people.name: Massa
people.summary: A lifting up, gift, one of the sons of Ishmael, the founder of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:14); a nomad tribe inhabiting the Arabian desert toward Babylonia.

people.name: Mattan
people.summary: A priest of Baal, slain before his altar during the reformation under Jehoiada (2 Kings 11:18).

people.name: Mattaniah
people.summary: A Levite, son of Heman, the chief of the ninth class of temple singers (1 Chr. 25:4, 16).

people.name: Mattaniah
people.summary: Father of Hashabiah.

people.name: Matthias
people.summary: Gift of God.

people.name: Medan
people.summary: A son of Jokshan, Abraham’s son by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:32). His descendants settled on the Syrian borders about the territory of Edom.

people.name: Mehetabel
people.summary: Wife of Hadad, one of the kings of Edom (Gen. 36:39).

people.name: Mehunim
people.summary: Habitations, (2 Chr. 26:7; R.V. “Meunim,” Vulg. Ammonitae), a people against whom Uzziah waged a successful war. This word is in Hebrew the plural of Ma’on, and thus denotes the Maonites who inhabited the country on the eastern side of the Wady el-Arabah.

people.name: Melech
people.summary: King, the second of Micah’s four sons (1 Chr. 8:35), and thus grandson of Mephibosheth.

people.name: Melzar
people.summary: Probably a Persian word meaning master of wine, i.e., chief butler; the title of an officer at the Babylonian court (Dan. 1:11, 16) who had charge of the diet of the Hebrew youths.

people.name: Mered
people.summary: Rebellion, one of the sons of Ezra, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:17).

people.name: Meshillemith
people.summary: A priest, the son of Immer (Neh. 11:13).

people.name: Meshullam
people.summary: A priest (1 Chr. 9:12).

people.name: Meshullam
people.summary: A Priest.

people.name: Mezahab
people.summary: Water of gold, the father of Matred (Gen. 36:39; 1 Chr. 1:50), and grandfather of Mehetabel, wife of Hadar, the last king of Edom.

people.name: Mibsam
people.summary: One of Ishmael’s twelve sons, and head of an Arab tribe (Gen. 25:13).

people.name: Mibzar
people.summary: Fortress, one of the Edomitish “dukes” descended from Esau (Gen. 36:42; 1 Chr. 1:53).

people.name: Micah
people.summary: “The Morasthite,” so called to distinguish him from Micaiah, the son of Imlah (1 Kings 22:8). He was a prophet of Judah, a contemporary of Isaiah (Micah 1:1), a native of Moresheth of Gath (1:14, 15).

people.name: Micha
people.summary: The son of Zabdi, a Levite of the family of Asaph (Neh. 11:17, 22).

people.name: Michaiah
people.summary: A Levite (Neh. 12:35).

people.name: Michaiah
people.summary: 2 Kings 22:12.

people.name: Michaiah
people.summary: The son of Gemariah.

people.name: Mishael
people.summary: A Levite; the eldest of the three sons of Uzziel (Ex. 6:22).

people.name: Mishma
people.summary: One of the sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:14), and founder of an Arab tribe.

people.name: Mishma
people.summary: A Simeonite (1 Chr. 4:25, 26).

people.name: Mispereth
people.summary: Number, one of the Jews who accompanied Zerubbabel from Babylon (Ezra 2:2); called also Mispereth (Neh. 7:7).

people.name: Mordecai
people.summary: One of the leaders of those who returned from exile with Zerrubabel in the days of Cyrus.

people.name: Naaman
people.summary: Head of Naamites.

people.name: Naarah
people.summary: A girl, the second of Ashur’s two wives, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:5, 6).

people.name: Nadab
people.summary: One of the sons of Shammai in the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 2:28, 30).

people.name: Nadab
people.summary: Son of Abiel.

people.name: Naharai
people.summary: Snorer, a Berothite, one of David’s heroes, and armour-bearer of Joab (1 Chr. 11:39).

people.name: Naphtuhim
people.summary: A Hamitic tribe descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:13). Others identify this word with Napata, the name of the city and territory on the southern frontier of Mizraim, the modern Meroe, at the great bend of the Nile at Soudan.

people.name: Neariah
people.summary: Sons: Hattush.

people.name: Nehemiah
people.summary: Ezra 2:2; Neh. 7:7.

people.name: Nekoda
people.summary: Father of Rezin.

people.name: Nergal-sharezer
people.summary: Another of the “princes,” who bore the title of “Rabmag.” He was one of those who were sent to release Jeremiah from prison (Jer. 39:13) by “the captain of the guard.”

people.name: Nethaniah
people.summary: The musician of David.

people.name: Neziah
people.summary: Victory; pure, Ezra 2:54; Neh. 7:56.

people.name: Nogah
people.summary: Splendour, one of David’s sons, born at Jerusalem (1 Chr. 3:7).

people.name: Obadiah
people.summary: A descendant of Saul (1 Chr. 8:38).

people.name: Oded
people.summary: The prophet.

people.name: Ohad
people.summary: United, or power, the third son of Simeon (Gen. 46:10).

people.name: Onam
people.summary: Sons of Shobal.

people.name: Onesimus
people.summary: Useful, a slave who, after robbing his master Philemon at Colosse, fled to Rome, where he was converted by the apostle Paul, who sent him back to his master with the epistle which bears his name.

people.name: Onesiphorus
people.summary: Bringing profit, an Ephesian Christian who showed great kindness to Paul at Rome. He served him in many things, and had oft refreshed him.

people.name: Ophir
people.summary: One of the sons of Joktan (Gen. 10:29).

people.name: Orpah
people.summary: Forelock or fawn, a Moabitess, the wife of Chilion (Ruth 1:4; 4:10).

people.name: Ozni
people.summary: Hearing, one of the sons of Gad; also called Ezbon (Gen. 46:16; Num. 26:16).

people.name: Pedaiah
people.summary: The father of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:17-19).

people.name: Pelaiah
