places.summary: A chaplet, the original seat of the Philistines (Deut. 2:23; Jer. 47:4; Amos 9:7). The name is found written in hieroglyphics in the temple of Kom Ombos in Upper Egypt.

places.name: Carchemish
places.summary: Fortress of Chemosh, a city on the west bank of the Euphrates (Jer. 46:2; 2 Chr. 35:20), not, as was once supposed, the Circesium at the confluence of the Chebar and the Euphrates, but a city considerably higher up the river, and commanding the ordinary passage of the Euphrates; probably identical with Hierapolis.

places.name: Daberath
places.summary: Pasture, a Levitical town of Issachar (Josh. 19:12; 21:28), near the border of Zebulum. It is the modern small village of Deburich, at the base of Mount Tabor.

places.name: Decapolis
places.summary: Ten cities=deka, ten, and polis, a city, a district on the east and south-east of the Sea of Galilee containing “ten cities,” which were chiefly inhabited by Greeks.

places.name: Ebenezer
places.summary: Stone of help, the memorial stone set up by Samuel to commemorate the divine assistance to Israel in their great battle against the Philistines, whom they totally routed (1 Sam. 7:7-12) at Aphek, in the neighbourhood of Mizpeh, in Benjamin, near the western entrance of the pass of Beth-horon.

places.name: Elath
places.summary: Grove; trees, (Deut. 2:8), also in plural form Eloth (1 Kings 9:26, etc.); called by the Greeks and Romans Elana; a city of Idumea, on the east, i.e., the Elanitic, gulf, or the Gulf of Akabah, of the Red Sea.

places.name: En-dor
places.summary: Fountain of Dor; i.e., “of the age”, a place in the territory of Issachar (Josh. 17:11) near the scene of the great victory which was gained by Deborah and Barak over Sisera and Jabin (comp. Ps. 83:9, 10).

places.name: Esau
places.summary: Hairy, Rebekah’s first-born twin son (Gen. 25:25). The name of Edom, “red”, was also given to him from his conduct in connection with the red lentil “pottage” for which he sold his birthright (30, 31).

places.name: Eshtemoa
places.summary: Obedience, a town in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 21:14; 1 Chr. 6:57), which was allotted, with the land round it, to the priests. It was frequented by David and his followers during their wanderings; and he sent presents of the spoil of the Amalekites to his friends there (1 Sam. 30:28).

places.name: Field
places.summary: A spot near Jerusalem (2 Kings 18:17; Isa. 36:2; 7:3), on the side of the highway west of the city, not far distant from the “upper pool” at the head of the valley of Hinnom.

places.name: fish gate
places.summary: Of cities, as of Jerusalem (Jer. 37:13; Neh. 1:3; 2:3; 3:3), of Sodom (Gen. 19:1), of Gaza (Judg. 16:3).

places.name: Gath-rimmon
places.summary: A Levitical city in the tribe of Dan (Josh. 19:45; 21:24; 1 Chr. 6:69).

places.name: Gebal
places.summary: A Phoenician city, not far from the sea coast, to the north of Beyrout (Ezek. 27:9); called by the Greeks Byblos. Now Jibeil.

places.name: Gederah
places.summary: The fortress; a fortified place, a town in the plain (shephelah) of Judah (Josh. 15:36). This is a very common Canaanite and Phoenician name.

places.name: Gennesaret
places.summary: A town of Naphtali, called Chinnereth (Josh. 19:35), sometimes in the plural form Chinneroth (11:2). In later times the name was gradually changed to Genezar and Gennesaret (Luke 5:1).

places.name: Gilboa
places.summary: Boiling spring, a mountain range, now Jebel Fukua’, memorable as the scene of Saul’s disastrous defeat by the Philistines. Here also his three sons were slain, and he himself died by his own hand (1 Sam. 28:4; 31:1-8; 2 Sam. 1:6-21; 21:12; 1 Chr. 10:1, 8).

places.name: Golgotha
places.summary: The common name of the spot where Jesus was crucified. It is interpreted by the evangelists as meaning “the place of a skull” (Matt. 27:33; Mark 15:22; John 19:17).

places.name: Goshen
places.summary: A district in Palestine (Josh. 10:41; 11:16).

places.name: Habor
places.summary: The united stream, or, according to others, with beautiful banks, the name of a river in Assyria, and also of the district through which it flowed (1 Chr. 5:26).

places.name: Hachilah
places.summary: The darksome hill, one of the peaks of the long ridge of el-Kolah, running out of the Ziph plateau, “on the south of Jeshimon” (i.e., of the “waste”), the district to which one looks down from the plateau of Ziph (1 Sam. 23:19).

places.name: Hadid
places.summary: Pointed, a place in the tribe of Benjamin near Lydda, or Lod, and Ono (Ezra 2:33; Neh. 7:37).

places.name: Halah
places.summary: A district of Media to which captive Israelites were transported by the Assyrian kings (2 Kings 17:6; 18:11; 1 Chr. 5:26). It lay along the banks of the upper Khabur, from its source to its junction with the Jerujer.

places.name: Harosheth-hagoyim
places.summary: (Judg. 4:2) or nations, a city near Hazor in Galilee of the Gentiles, or Upper Galilee, in the north of Palestine. It was here that Jabin’s great army was marshalled before it went forth into the great battlefield of Esdraelon to encounter the army of Israel, by which it was routed and put to flight (Judg. 4).

places.name: Hazor
places.summary: A district in Arabia (Jer. 49:28-33), supposed by some to be Jetor, i.e., Ituraea.

places.name: Hena
places.summary: One of the cities of Mesopotamia destroyed by sennacherib (2 Kings 18:34; 19:13).

places.name: Ibleam
places.summary: People-waster, a city assigned to Manasseh (Josh. 17:11), from which the Israelites, however, could not expel the Canaanites (Judg. 1:27). It is also called Bileam (1 Chr. 6:70).

places.name: Ijon
places.summary: A ruin, a city of Naphtali, captured by Ben-hadad of Syria at the instance of Asa (1 Kings 15:20), and afterwards by Tiglath-pileser of Assyria (2 Kings 15:29) in the reign of Pekah; now el-Khiam.

places.name: Ivvah
places.summary: Overturning, a city of the Assyrians, whence colonists were brought to Samaria (2 Kings 18:34; 19:13).

places.name: Jokneam
places.summary: Gathered by the people, (Josh. 19:11; 21:34), a city “of Carmel” (12:22), i.e., on Carmel, allotted with its suburbs to the Merarite Levites.

places.name: Kabzeel
places.summary: Gathering of God, a city in the extreme south of Judah, near to Idumaea (Josh. 15:21), the birthplace of Benaiah, one of David’s chief warriors (2 Sam. 23:20; 1 Chr. 11:22).

places.name: Lehi
places.summary: A jawbone, a place in the tribe of Judah where Samson achieved a victory over the Philistines (Judg. 15:9, 14, 16), slaying a thousand of them with the jawbone of an ass.

places.name: Lo-debar
places.summary: No pasture, (2 Sam. 17:27), a town in Gilead not far from Mahanaim, north of the Jabbok (9:4, 5).

places.name: Lydda
places.summary: A town in the tribe of Ephraim, mentioned only in the New Testament (Acts 9:32, 35, 38) as the scene of Peter’s miracle in healing the paralytic AEneas.

places.name: Magog
places.summary: Region of Gog, the second of the “sons” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2; 1 Chr. 1:5). In Ezekiel (38:2; 39:6) it is the name of a nation, probably some Scythian or Tartar tribe descended from Japheth.

places.name: Marah
places.summary: Bitterness, a fountain at the sixth station of the Israelites (Ex. 15:23, 24; Num. 33:8) whose waters were so bitter that they could not drink them.

places.name: Meribah-kadesh
places.summary: Holy, or Kadesh-Barnea, sacred desert of wandering, a place on the south-eastern border of Palestine, about 165 miles from Horeb. It lay in the “wilderness” or “desert of Zin” (Gen. 14:7; Num. 13:3-26; 14:29-33; 20:1; 27:14), on the border of Edom (20:16).

places.name: Miletus
places.summary: (Miletum, 2 Tim. 4:20), a seaport town and the ancient capital of Ionia, about 36 miles south of Ephesus. On his voyage from Greece to Syria, Paul touched at this port, and delivered that noble and pathetic address to the elders (“presbyters,” ver. 28) of Ephesus recorded in Acts 20:15-35.

places.name: Nebo
places.summary: The “children of Nebo” (Ezra 2:29; Neh. 7:33) were of those who returned from Babylon.

places.name: Nehelam
places.summary: The name given to a false prophet Shemaiah, who went with the captives to Babylon (Jer. 29:24, 31, 32). The origin of the name is unknown.

places.name: Olivet
places.summary: so called from the olive trees with which its sides are clothed, is a mountain ridge on the east of Jerusalem ( 1 Kings 11:7 ; Ezekiel 11:23 ; Zechariah 14:4 ), from which it is separated by the valley of Kidron.

places.name: Perga
places.summary: The capital of Pamphylia, on the coast of Asia Minor. Paul and his companions landed at this place from Cyprus on their first missionary journey (Acts 13:13, 14), and here Mark forsook the party and returned to Jerusalem.

places.name: Phenicia
places.summary: (Acts 21:2) = Phenice (11:19; 15:3; R.V., Phoenicia), Gr. phoinix, “a palm”, the land of palm-trees; a strip of land of an average breadth of about 20 miles along the shores of the Mediterranean, from the river Eleutherus in the north to the promotory of Carmel in the south, about 120 miles in length.

places.name: Phrygia
places.summary: Dry, an irregular and ill-defined district in Asia Minor. It was divided into two parts, the Greater Phrygia on the south, and the Lesser Phrygia on the west.

places.name: Pi-hahiroth
places.summary: Place where the reeds grow (LXX. and Copt. read “farmstead”), the name of a place in Egypt where the children of Israel encamped (Ex. 14:2, 9), how long is uncertain.

places.name: Pontus
places.summary: A province of Asia Minor, stretching along the southern coast of the Euxine Sea, corresponding nearly to the modern province of Trebizond. In the time of the apostles it was a Roman province.

places.name: Put
places.summary: Phut is placed between Egypt and Canaan in Gen. 10:6, and elsewhere we find the people of Phut described as mercenaries in the armies of Egypt and Tyre (Jer. 46:9; Ezek. 30:5; 27:10).

places.name: Rahab
places.summary: Insolence; pride, a poetical name applied to Egypt in Ps. 87:4; 89:10; Isa. 51:9, as “the proud one.”

places.name: Ramoth
places.summary: Heights of Gilead, a city of refuge on the east of Jordan; called “Ramoth in Gilead” (Deut. 4:43; Josh. 20:8; 21:38). Here Ahab, who joined Jehoshaphat in an endeavour to rescue it from the hands of the king of Syria, was mortally wounded (1 Kings 22:1-36).

places.name: Rimmon
places.summary: “Rock of,” to which the Benjamites fled (Judg. 20:45, 47; 21:13), and where they maintained themselves for four months after the fearful battle at Gibeah, in which they were almost exterminated, 600 only surviving out of about 27,000.

places.name: Sardis
places.summary: The metropolis of Lydia in Asia Minor. It stood on the river Pactolus, at the foot of mount Tmolus. Here was one of the seven Asiatic churches (Rev. 3:1-6).

places.name: Sela
places.summary: Se’lah, rock, the capital of Edom, situated in the great valley extending from the Dead Sea to the Red Sea (2 Kings 14:7). It was near Mount Hor, close by the desert of Zin.

places.name: Shunem
places.summary: Two resting-places, a little village in the tribe of Issachar, to the north of Jezreel and south of Mount Gilboa (Josh. 19:18), where the Philistines encamped when they came against Saul (1 Sam. 28:4), and where Elisha was hospitably entertained by a rich woman of the place.

places.name: Siloam
places.summary: Sent or sending. Here a notable miracle was wrought by our Lord in giving sight to the blind (John 9:7-11).

places.name: Sirion
places.summary: A breastplate, the Sidonian name of Hermon, Deut. 3:9; Ps. 29:6.

places.name: Syene
places.summary: Opening (Ezek. 29:10; 30:6), a town of Egypt, on the borders of Ethiopia, now called Assouan, on the right bank of the Nile, notable for its quarries of beautiful red granite called “syenite.”

places.name: Tappuah
places.summary: A town on the border of Ephraim (Josh. 16:8).

places.name: Tema
places.summary: South; desert, one of the sons of Ishmael, and father of a tribe so called (Gen. 25:15; 1 Chr. 1:30; Job 6:19; Isa. 21:14; Jer. 25:23) which settled at a place to which he gave his name, some 250 miles south-east of Edom, on the route between Damascus and Mecca, in the northern part of the Arabian peninsula, toward the Syrian desert; the modern Teyma’.

places.name: Uz
places.summary: Where Job lived (1:1; Jer. 25:20; Lam. 4:21), probably somewhere to the east or south-east of Palestine and north of Edom.

places.name: vale of Siddim
places.summary: Valley of the broad plains, “which is the salt sea” (Gen. 14:3, 8, 10), between Engedi and the cities of the plain, at the south end of the Dead Sea.

places.name: valley of Elah
places.summary: Valley of, where the Israelites were encamped when David killed Goliath (1 Sam. 17:2, 19). It was near Shochoh of Judah and Azekah (17:1). It is the modern Wady es-Sunt, i.e., “valley of the acacia.”

places.name: valley of Hinnom
places.summary: A deep, narrow ravine separating Mount Zion from the so-called “Hill of Evil Counsel.” It took its name from “some ancient hero, the son of Hinnom.”

places.name: valley of Jezreel
places.summary: Lying on the northern side of the city, between the ridges of Gilboa and Moreh, an offshoot of Esdraelon, running east to the Jordan (Josh. 17:16; Judg. 6:33; Hos. 1:5).

places.name: Zanoah
places.summary: A town in the low country or shephelah of Judah, near Zorah (Josh. 15:34). It was re-occupied after the return from the Captivity (Neh. 11:30).

places.name: Abdon
places.summary: One of the “sons” of Shashak (1 Chr. 8:23).

places.name: Abel-beth-maacah
places.summary: Meadow of the house of Maachah, a city in the north of Palestine, in the neighbourhood of Dan and Ijon, in the tribe of Naphtali. It was a place of considerable strength and importance.

places.name: Abronah
places.summary: R.V., one of Israel’s halting-places in the desert (Num. 33:34, 35), just before Ezion-gaber.

places.name: Achzib
places.summary: A town in the Shephelah, or plain country of Judah (Josh. 15:44); probably the same as Chezib of Gen. 38:5 = Ain Kezbeh.

places.name: Achzib
places.summary: A Phoenician city (the Gr. Ecdippa), always retained in their possession though assigned to the tribe of Asher (Josh. 19:29; Judg. 1:31).

places.name: Adummim
places.summary: The red ones, a place apparently on the road between Jericho and Jerusalem, “on the south side of the torrent” Wady Kelt, looking toward Gilgal, mentioned Josh. 15:7; 18:17.

places.name: Akeldama
places.summary: The name which the Jews gave in their proper tongue, i.e., in Aramaic, to the field which was purchased with the money which had been given to the betrayer of our Lord.

places.name: Almon-diblathaim
places.summary: Two cakes, a city of Moab, on the east of the Dead Sea (Num. 33:46; Jer. 48:22).

places.name: Alush
places.summary: One of the places, the last before Rephidim, at which the Hebrews rested on their way to Sinai (Num. 33:13, 14).

places.name: Anab
places.summary: Grape-town, one of the cities in the mountains of Judah, from which Joshua expelled the Anakim (Josh. 11:21; 15:50). It still retains its ancient name.

places.name: Aphek
places.summary: A city of the tribe of Asher. It was the scene of the licentious worship of the Syrian Aphrodite.

places.name: Ararat
places.summary: Sacred land or high land, the name of a country on one of the mountains of which the ark rested after the Flood subsided (Gen. 8:4). The “mountains” mentioned were probably the Kurdish range of South Armenia.

places.name: Arvad
places.summary: Wandering, (Ezek. 27:8), a small island and city on the coast of Syria, mentioned as furnishing mariners and soldiers for Tyre. The inhabitants were called Arvadites.

places.name: Assos
places.summary: A sea-port town of Proconsular Asia, in the district of Mysia, on the north shore of the Gulf of Adramyttium. Paul came hither on foot along the Roman road from Troas (Acts 20:13, 14), a distance of 20 miles.

places.name: Atad
places.summary: Buckthorn, a place where Joseph and his brethren, when on their way from Egypt to Hebron with the remains of their father Jacob, made for seven days a “great and very sore lamentation.”

places.name: Ataroth
places.summary: A city east of Jordan, not far from Gilead (Num. 32:3).

places.name: Ataroth
places.summary: A town on the border of Ephraim and Benjamin (Josh. 16:2, 7), called also Ataroth-adar (16:5).

places.name: Azmaveth
places.summary: A town in the tribe of Judah, near Jerusalem (Neh. 12:29; Ezra 2:24).

places.name: Baal-perazim
places.summary: Baal having rents, bursts, or destructions, the scene of a victory gained by David over the Philistines (2 Sam. 5:20; 1 Chr. 14:11). Called Mount Perazim (Isa. 28:21).

places.name: Baalath
places.summary: A town of the tribe of Dan (Josh. 19:44). It was fortified by Solomon (1 Kings 9:18; 2 Chr. 8:6).

places.name: Babel
places.summary: The name given to the tower which the primitive fathers of our race built in the land of Shinar after the Deluge (Gen. 11:1-9). Their object in building this tower was probably that it might be seen as a rallying-point in the extensive plain of Shinar, to which they had emigrated from the uplands of Armenia, and so prevent their being scattered abroad.

places.name: Bamoth
places.summary: Heights, the forty-seventh station of the Israelites (Num. 21:19, 20) in the territory of the Moabites.

places.name: Bamoth-baal
places.summary: Heights of Baal, a place on the river Arnon, or in the plains through which it flows, east of Jordan (Josh. 13:17; comp. Num. 21:28).

places.name: Beautiful gate
places.summary: The name of one of the gates of the temple (Acts 3:2). It is supposed to have been the door which led from the court of the Gentiles to the court of the women.

places.name: Beer-lahai-roi
places.summary: I.e., “the well of him that liveth and seeth me,” or, as some render it, “the well of the vision of life”, the well where the Lord met with Hagar (Gen. 16:7-14).

places.name: Bela
places.summary: A city on the shore of the Dead Sea, not far from Sodom, called also Zoar. It was the only one of the five cities that was spared at Lot’s intercession (Gen. 19:20, 23).

places.name: Bene-jaakan
places.summary: Children of Jaakan (Num. 33:31, 32), the same as Beeroth.

places.name: Berea
places.summary: A city of Macedonia to which Paul with Silas and Timotheus went when persecuted at Thessalonica (Acts 17:10, 13), and from which also he was compelled to withdraw, when he fled to the sea-coast and thence sailed to Athens (14, 15).

places.name: Beth-anath
places.summary: House of response, one of the fenced cities of Naphtali (Josh. 19:38).

places.name: Beth-haccherem
places.summary: House of a vineyard, a place in the tribe of Judah (Neh. 3:14) where the Benjamites were to set up a beacon when they heard the trumpet against the invading army of the Babylonians (Jer. 6:1).

places.name: Beth-maacah
places.summary: Meadow of the house of Maachah, a city in the north of Palestine, in the neighbourhood of Dan and Ijon, in the tribe of Naphtali. It was a place of considerable strength and importance.

places.name: Beth-millo
places.summary: In Judg. 9:6, 20 it is the name of a rampart in Shechem, probably the “tower of Shechem” (9:46, 49).

places.name: Beth-nimrah
places.summary: now Beth-Nimrah

places.name: Beth-shemesh
places.summary: One of the fenced cities of Naphtali (Josh. 19:38), between Mount Tabor and the Jordan. Now Khurbet Shema, 3 miles west of Safed.

places.name: Beth-togarmah
places.summary: region

places.name: Bethel
places.summary: A town in the south of Judah (Josh. 8:17; 12:16).

places.name: Bezek
places.summary: The residence of Adoni-bezek, in the lot of Judah (Judg. 1:5). It was in the mountains, not far from Jerusalem.

places.name: Bithynia
places.summary: A province in Asia Minor, to the south of the Euxine and Propontis. Christian congregations were here formed at an early time (1 Pet. 1:1). Paul was prevented by the Spirit from entering this province (Acts 16:7).

places.name: Bochim
places.summary: Weepers, a place where the angel of the Lord reproved the Israelites for entering into a league with the people of the land. This caused them bitterly to weep, and hence the name of the place (Judg. 2:1, 5).

places.name: brook Kidron
places.summary: The black torrent, the brook flowing through the ravine below the eastern wall of Jerusalem (John 18:1).

places.name: Caesarea Philippi
places.summary: A city on the northeast of the marshy plain of el-Huleh, 120 miles north of Jerusalem, and 20 miles north of the Sea of Galilee, at the “upper source” of the Jordan, and near the base of Mount Hermon.

places.name: Calah
places.summary: One of the most ancient cities of Assyria. “Out of that land he [i.e., Nimrod] went forth into Assyria, and built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, and Calah, and Resen” (Gen. 10:11, R.V.).

places.name: Calneh
places.summary: Fort, one of the four cities founded by Nimrod (Gen. 10:10). It is the modern Niffer, a lofty mound of earth and rubbish situated in the marshes on the left, i.e., the east, bank of the Euphrates, but 30 miles distant from its present course, and about 60 miles south-south-east from Babylon.

places.name: Cappadocia
places.summary: The easternmost and the largest province of Asia Minor. Christianity very early penetrated into this country (1 Pet. 1:1).

places.name: Cenchreae
places.summary: Millet, the eastern harbour of Corinth, from which it was distant about 9 miles east, and the outlet for its trade with the Asiatic shores of the Mediterranean.

places.name: Cherith
places.summary: A cutting; separation; a gorge, a torrent-bed or winter-stream, a “brook,” in whose banks the prophet Elijah hid himself during the early part of the three years’ drought (1 Kings 17:3, 5).

places.name: Cherub
places.summary: Plural cherubim, the name of certain symbolical figures frequently mentioned in Scripture. They are first mentioned in connection with the expulsion of our first parents from Eden (Gen. 3:24).

places.name: Chinneroth
places.summary: Lyre, the singular form of the word (Deut. 3:17; Josh. 19:35), which is also used in the plural form, Chinneroth, the name of a fenced city which stood near the shore of the lake of Galilee, a little to the south of Tiberias.

places.name: Chorazin
places.summary: Named along with Bethsaida and Capernaum as one of the cities in which our Lord’s “mighty works” were done, and which was doomed to woe because of signal privileges neglected (Matt. 11:21; Luke 10:13).

places.name: Dinhabah
places.summary: Robbers’ den, an Edomitish city, the capital of king Bela (Gen. 36:32).

places.name: Dophkah
places.summary: Knocking, an encampment of the Israelites in the wilderness (Num. 33:12).

places.name: Dothan
places.summary: Two wells, a famous pasture-ground where Joseph found his brethren watching their flocks. Here, at the suggestion of Judah, they sold him to the Ishmaelite merchants (Gen. 37:17).

places.name: Eglath-shelishiyah
places.summary: Heb. ‘eglah, (Deut. 21:4, 6; Jer. 46:20).

places.name: Ellasar
places.summary: The oak or heap of Assyria, a territory in Asia of which Arioch was king (Gen. 14:1, 9). It is supposed that the old Chaldean town of Larsa was the metropolis of this kingdom, situated nearly half-way between Ur (now Mugheir) and Erech, on the left bank of the Euphrates.

places.name: En-gannim
places.summary: A city on the border of Machar (Josh. 19:21), allotted to the Gershonite Levites (21:29). It is identified with the modern Jenin, a large and prosperous town of about 4,000 inhabitants, situated 15 miles south of Mount Tabor, through which the road from Jezreel to Samaria and Jerusalem passes.

places.name: En-shemesh
places.summary: Fountain of the sun a spring which formed one of the landmarks on the boundary between Judah and Benjamin (Josh. 15:7; 18:17). It was between the “ascent of Adummim” and the spring of En-rogel, and hence was on the east of Jerusalem and of the Mount of Olives.

places.name: Ephrathah
places.summary: The ancient name of Bethlehem in Judah (Gen. 35:16, 19; 48:7). In Ruth 1:2 it is called “Bethlehem-Judah,” but the inhabitants are called “Ephrathites;” in Micah 5:2, “Bethlehem-Ephratah;” in Matt. 2:6, “Bethlehem in the land of Judah.”

places.name: Erech
places.summary: (LXX., “Orech”), length, or Moon-town, one of the cities of Nimrod’s kingdom in the plain of Shinar (Gen. 10:10); the Orchoe of the Greeks and Romans.

places.name: Etam
places.summary: A village of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:32). Into some cleft (“top,” A.V.,; R.V., “cleft”) of a rock here Samson retired after his slaughter of the Philistines (Judg. 15:8, 11).

places.name: Forest of Ephraim
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1273 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Galeed
places.summary: Heap of witness, the name of the pile of stones erected by Jacob and Laban to mark the league of friendship into which they entered with each other (Gen. 31:47, 48).

places.name: Gallim
places.summary: Heaps, (1 Sam. 25:44; Isa. 10:30). The native place of Phalti, to whom Michal was given by Saul.

places.name: gate of Ephraim
places.summary: One of the gates of Jerusalem (2 Kings 14:13; 2 Chr. 25:23), on the side of the city looking toward Ephraim, the north side.

places.name: Gath-hepher
places.summary: Wine-press of the well, a town of Lower Galilee, about 5 miles from Nazareth; the birthplace of Jonah (2 Kings 14:25); the same as Gittah-hepher (Josh. 19:13).

places.name: Gedor
places.summary: A town apparently in Benjamin (1 Chr. 12:7), the same probably as Geder (Josh. 12:13).

places.name: Gethsemane
places.summary: Oil-press, the name of an olive-yard at the foot of the Mount of Olives, to which Jesus was wont to retire (Luke 22:39) with his disciples, and which is specially memorable as being the scene of his agony (Mark 14:32; John 18:1; Luke 22:44).

places.name: Gibeah
places.summary: (Josh. 15:57, R.V. marg.), a city on Mount Ephraim which had been given to Phinehas (24:33 “hill,” A.V.; R.V. marg. and Heb., “Gibeah.”). Here Eleazar the son of Aaron was buried.

places.name: Giloh
places.summary: Exile, a city in the south-west part of the hill-country of Judah (Josh. 15:51). It was the native place or residence of the traitor Ahithophel “the Gilonite” (Josh. 15:51; 2 Sam. 15:12), and where he committed suicide (17:23).

places.name: Gittaim
places.summary: Two wine-presses, (2 Sam. 4:3; Neh. 11:33), a town probably in Benjamin to which the Beerothites fled.

places.name: Gob
places.summary: A pit, a place mentioned in 2 Sam. 21:18, 19; called also Gezer, in 1 Chr. 20:4.

places.name: Hammath
places.summary: Warm springs, one of the “fenced cities” of Naphtali (Josh. 19:35).

places.name: Hammon
places.summary: A town in the tribe of Asher, near Zidon (Josh. 19:28), identified with ‘Ain Hamul.

places.name: Haradah
places.summary: Fright; fear, the twenty-fifth station of the Israelites in their wanderings (Num. 33:24).

places.name: Harod
places.summary: An epithet applied to two of David’s heroes (2 Sam. 23:25).

places.name: Hashmonah
places.summary: Fatness, the thirtieth halting-place of the Israelites during their wanderings in the wilderness, not far from Mount Hor (Num. 33:29, 30).

places.name: Hauran
places.summary: Cave-land, mentioned only in Ezek. 47:16, 18. It was one of the ancient divisions of Bashan, and lay on the south-east of Gaulanitis or the Jaulan, and on the south of Lejah, extending from the Arnon to the Hieromax.

places.name: Havilah
places.summary: A district in Arabia-Felix. It is uncertain whether the tribe gave its name to this region or derived its name from it, and whether it was originally a Cushite (Gen. 10:7) or a Joktanite tribe (10:29; comp. 25:18), or whether there were both a Cushite and a Joktanite Havilah.

places.name: Helam
places.summary: Place of abundance, a place on the east of Jordan and west of the Euphrates where David gained a great victory over the Syrian army (2 Sam. 10:16), which was under the command of Shobach.

places.name: Helkath
places.summary: Smoothness, a town of Asher, on the east border (Josh. 19:25; 21:31); called also Hukok (1 Chr. 6:75).

places.name: Hethlon
places.summary: Wrapped up, a place on the north border of Palestine.

places.name: horse gate
places.summary: A gate in the wall of Jerusalem, at the west end of the bridge, leading from Zion to the temple (Neh. 3:28; Jer. 31:40).

places.name: India
places.summary: Occurs only in Esther 1:1 and 8:9, where the extent of the dominion of the Persian king is described. The country so designated here is not the peninsula of Hindustan, but the country surrounding the Indus, the Punjab.

places.name: Janoah
places.summary: A town on the north-eastern border of Ephraim, in the Jordan valley (Josh. 16:6, 7).

places.name: Javan
places.summary: from harper; http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ionia

places.name: Juttah
places.summary: Extended, a Levitical city in the mountains or hill-country of Judah (Josh. 15:55; 21:16). Its modern name is Yutta, a place about 5 1/2 miles south of Hebron.

places.name: Kain
places.summary: A town of the Kenites, a branch of the Midianites (Josh. 15:57), on the east edge of the mountain above Engedi; probably the “nest in a rock” mentioned by Balaam (Num. 24:21).

places.name: Kanah
places.summary: A stream forming the boundary between Ephraim and Manasseh, from the Mediterranean eastward to Tappuah (Josh. 16:8). It has been identified with the sedgy streams that constitute the Wady Talaik, which enters the sea between Joppa and Caesarea.

places.name: Kehelathah
places.summary: Assembly, one of the stations of the Israelites in the desert (Num. 33:22, 23).

places.name: Kenath
places.summary: Possession, a city of Gilead. It was captured by Nobah, who called it by his own name (Num. 32:42).

places.name: Kerioth
places.summary: A city of Moab (Jer. 48:24, 41), called Kirioth (Amos 2:2).

places.name: Kir-hareseth
places.summary: Built fortress, a city and fortress of Moab, the modern Kerak, a small town on the brow of a steep hill about 6 miles from Rabbath-Moab and 10 miles from the Dead Sea; called also Kir-haresh, Kir-hareseth, Kir-heres (Isa. 16:7, 11; Jer. 48:31, 36).

places.name: Kishion
places.summary: Hardness, a city of Issachar assigned to the Gershonite Levites (Josh. 19:20), the same as Kishon (21:28).

places.name: Kue
places.summary: from tyndale

places.name: Libnah
places.summary: One of the stations of the Israelites in the wilderness (Num. 33:20, 21).

places.name: Libya
places.summary: The country of the Ludim (Gen. 10:13), Northern Africa, a large tract lying along the Mediterranean, to the west of Egypt (Acts 2:10).

places.name: Luhith
places.summary: Made of boards, a Moabitish place between Zoar and Horonaim (Isa. 15:5; Jer. 48:5).

places.name: Madmannah
places.summary: Dunghill, the modern el-Minyay, 15 miles south-south-west of Gaza (Josh. 15:31; 1 Chr. 2:49), in the south of Judah. The Pal.

places.name: Madon
places.summary: Strife, a Canaanitish city in the north of Palestine (Josh. 11:1; 12:19), whose king was slain by Joshua; perhaps the ruin Madin, near Hattin, some 5 miles west of Tiberias.

places.name: Mahaneh-dan
places.summary: Judg. 18:12 = “camp of Dan” 13:25 (R.V., “Mahaneh-dan”), a place behind (i.e., west of) Kirjath-jearim, where the six hundred Danites from Zorah and Eshtaol encamped on their way to capture the city of Laish, which they rebuilt and called “Dan, after the name of their father” (18:11-31).

places.name: Makheloth
places.summary: Assemblies, a station of the Israelites in the desert (Num. 33:25, 26).

places.name: Masrekah
places.summary: Vineyard of noble vines, a place in Idumea, the native place of Samlah, one of the Edomitish kings (Gen. 36:36; 1 Chr. 1:47).

places.name: Mattanah
places.summary: A gift, a station of the Israelites (Num. 21:18, 19) between the desert and the borders of Moab, in the Wady Waleh.

places.name: Meribah
places.summary: One of the names given by Moses to the fountain in the desert of Sin, near Rephidim, which issued from the rock in Horeb, which he smote by the divine command, “because of the chiding of the children of Israel” (Ex. 17:1-7).

places.name: Merom
places.summary: Height, a lake in Northern Palestine through which the Jordan flows. It was the scene of the third and last great victory gained by Joshua over the Canaanites (Josh. 11:5-7).

places.name: Michmas
places.summary: Something hidden, a town of Benjamin (Ezra 2:27), east of Bethel and south of Migron, on the road to Jerusalem (Isa. 10:28). It lay on the line of march of an invading army from the north, on the north side of the steep and precipitous Wady es-Suweinit (“valley of the little thorn-tree” or “the acacia”), and now bears the name of Mukhmas.

places.name: Michmethath
places.summary: Hiding-place, a town in the northern border of Ephraim and Manasseh, and not far west of Jordan (Josh. 16:6; 17:7).

places.name: Migron
places.summary: Precipice or landslip, a place between Aiath and Michmash (Isa. 10:28).

places.name: Minnith
places.summary: Distribution, an Ammonitish town (Judg. 11:33) from which wheat was exported to Tyre (Ezek. 27:17). It was probably somewhere in the Mishor or table-land on the east of Jordan.

places.name: Mishal
places.summary: A city of the tribe of Asher (Josh. 21:30; 1 Chr. 6:74).

places.name: Misrephoth-maim
places.summary: Burning of waters, supposed to be salt-pans, or lime-kilns, or glass-factories, a place to which Joshua pursued a party of Canaanites after the defeat of Jabin (Josh. 11:8).

places.name: Mithkah
places.summary: Sweetness, one of the stations of the Israelites in the wilderness (Num. 33:28, 29).

places.name: Moreh
places.summary: A Canaanite probably who inhabited the district south of Shechem, between Mounts Ebal and Gerizim, and gave his name to the “plain” there (Gen. 12:6).

places.name: Moseroth
places.summary: Bonds, one of the stations in the wilderness (Num. 33:30, 31), probably the same as Mosera.

places.name: mount Halak
places.summary: Smooth; bald, a hill at the southern extremity of Canaan (Josh. 11:17). It is referred to as if it were a landmark in that direction, being prominent and conspicuous from a distance.

places.name: mount Hor
places.summary: One of the marks of the northern boundary of Palestine (Num. 34:7, 8). Nowhere else mentioned.

places.name: mount Nebo
places.summary: A mountain in the land of Moab from which Moses looked for the first and the last time on the Promised Land (Deut. 32:49; 34:1). It has been identified with Jebel Nebah, on the eastern shore of the Dead Sea, near its northern end, and about 5 miles south-west of Heshbon.

places.name: mount Paran
places.summary: Probably the hilly region or upland wilderness on the north of the desert of Paran forming the southern boundary of the Promised Land (Deut. 33:2; Hab. 3:3).

places.name: mount Shapher
places.summary: Brightness, one of the stations where Israel encamped in the wilderness (Num. 33:23, 24).

places.name: Mysia
places.summary: A province in the north-west of Asia Minor.

places.name: Nahalal
places.summary: Pasture, a city in Zebulun on the border of Issachar (Josh. 19:15), the same as Nahalol (Judg. 1:30). It was given to the Levites.

places.name: Nephtoah
places.summary: Opened, a fountain and a stream issuing from it on the border between Judah and Benjamin (Josh. 15:8, 9; 18:15). It has been identified with ‘Ain Lifta, a spring about 2 1/2 miles north-west of Jerusalem.

places.name: Nimrim
places.summary: The stream of the leopards, a stream in Moab (Isa. 15:6; Jer. 48:34); probably the modern Wady en-Nemeirah, a rich, verdant spot at the south-eastern end of the Dead Sea.

places.name: Nobah
places.summary: The name given to Kenath by Nobah when he conquered it.

places.name: Paphos
places.summary: The capital of the island of Cyprus, and therefore the residence of the Roman governor. It was visited by Paul and Barnabas on their first missionary tour (Acts 13:6).

places.name: Pekod
places.summary: Probably a place in Babylonia (Jer. 50:21; Ezek. 23:23).

places.name: Pelusium
places.summary: “Sin against the Holy Ghost”, or a “sin unto death” (Matt. 12:31, 32; 1 John 5:16), which amounts to a wilful rejection of grace.

places.name: Pergamum
places.summary: The chief city of Mysia, in Asia Minor. One of the “seven churches” was planted here (Rev. 1:11; 2:17). It was noted for its wickedness, insomuch that our Lord says “Satan’s seat” was there.

places.name: Pethor
places.summary: Interpretation of dreams, identified with Pitru, on the west bank of the Euphrates, a few miles south of the Hittite capital of Carchemish (Num. 22:5, “which is by the river of the land of the children of [the god] Ammo”).

places.name: Philadelphia
places.summary: Brotherly love, a city of Lydia in Asia Minor, about 25 miles south-east of Sardis. It was the seat of one of the “seven churches” (Rev. 3:7-12).

places.name: Pisidia
places.summary: A district in Asia Minor, to the north of Pamphylia. The Taurus range of mountains extends through it.

places.name: plain of Jordan
places.summary: The Jabbok or Wady Zerka, formerly the northern boundary of Ammon.

places.name: Ramah
places.summary: The same as Ramoth-gilead, 2 Kings 8:29; 2 Chr. 22:6.

places.name: Ramoth
places.summary: Heights.

places.name: Rehob
places.summary: The same, probably, as Beth-rehob (2 Sam. 10:6, 8; Judg. 18:28), a place in the north of Palestine (Num. 13:21).

places.name: Rehoboth
places.summary: An ancient city on the Euphrates (Gen. 36:37; 1 Chr. 1:48), “Rehoboth by the river.”

places.name: Rezeph
places.summary: Solid; a stone, (2 Kings 19:12; Isa. 37:12), a fortress near Haran, probably on the west of the Euphrates, conquered by Sennacherib.

places.name: Rissah
places.summary: Heap of ruins; dew, a station of the Israelites in the wilderness (Num. 33:21, 22).

places.name: Rithmah
places.summary: Wild broom, a station in the wilderness (Num. 33:18, 19), the “broom valley,” or “valley of broombushes,” the place apparently of the original encampment of Israel, near Kadesh.

places.name: Rogelim
places.summary: Fullers, a town of Gilead, the residence of Barzillai the Gileadite (2 Sam. 17:27; 19:31), probably near to Mahanaim.

places.name: sea of the plain
places.summary: water

places.name: sea of Tiberias
places.summary: water

places.name: Seba
places.summary: The name of a country and nation (Isa. 43:3; 45:14) mentioned along with Egypt and Ethiopia, and therefore probably in north-eastern Africa.

places.name: Second Quarter
places.summary: Heb. mishneh (2 Kings 22:14; 2 Chr. 34:22), rendered in Revised Version “second quarter”, the residence of the prophetess Huldah. The Authorized Version followed the Jewish commentators, who, following the Targum, gave the Hebrew word its post-Biblical sense, as if it meant a place of instruction.

places.name: Sela-hammahlekoth
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1276 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Shaalbim
places.summary: now Salbit

places.name: Shaaraim
places.summary: A city in the plain of Judah (1 Sam. 17:52); called also Sharaim (Josh. 15:36).

places.name: Shamir
places.summary: The residence of Tola, one of the judges, on Mount Ephraim (Judg. 10:1, 2).

places.name: Shepham
places.summary: A treeless place, Num. 34:10, 11: “The coast shall go down from Shepham to Riblah.”

places.name: Shihor
places.summary: (correctly Shi’hor) black; dark the name given to the river Nile in Isa. 23:3; Jer. 2:18.

places.name: Shimron
places.summary: Watch-post, an ancient city of the Canaanites; with its villages, allotted to Zebulun (Josh. 19:15); now probably Semunieh, on the northern edge of the plain of Esdraelon, 5 miles west of Nazareth.

places.name: Smyrna
places.summary: Myrrh, an ancient city of Ionia, on the western coast of Asia Minor, about 40 miles to the north of Ephesus. It is now the chief city of Anatolia, having a mixed population of about 200,000, of whom about one-third are professed Christians.

places.name: Solomon's Portico
places.summary: (John 10:23; Acts 3:11; 5:12), a colonnade, or cloister probably, on the eastern side of the temple.

places.name: Spain
places.summary: Paul expresses his intention (Rom. 15:24, 28) to visit Spain.

places.name: Taberah
places.summary: Burning, a place in the wilderness of Paran, where the “fire of the Lord” consumed the murmuring Israelites (Num. 11:3; Deut. 9:22).

places.name: Tamar
places.summary: now Kurnub; from New Bible Dictionary

places.name: Tel-harsha
places.summary: near the sea

places.name: Tel-melah
places.summary: from tyndale

places.name: Telassar
places.summary: Or Thelasar, (Isa. 37:12; 2 Kings 19:12), a province in the south-east of Assyria, probably in Babylonia.

places.name: Terah
places.summary: Stopping; station, an encampment of the Hebrews in the wilderness (Num. 33:27, 28).

places.name: Thebez
places.summary: Brightness, a place some 11 miles north-east of Shechem, on the road to Scythopolis, the modern Tabas.

places.name: Hiddekel
places.summary: Called by the Accadians id Idikla; i.e., “the river of Idikla”, the third of the four rivers of Paradise (Gen. 2:14). Gesenius interprets the word as meaning “the rapid Tigris.”

places.name: Timnath-serah
places.summary: Remaining portion, the city of Joshua in the hill country of Ephraim, the same as Timnath-heres (Josh. 19:50; 24:30). “Of all sites I have seen,” says Lieut.

places.name: Tob
places.summary: A district on the east of Jodan, about 13 miles south-east of the Sea of Galilee, to which Jephthah fled from his brethren (Judg. 11:3, 5). It was on the northern boundary of Perea, between Syria and the land of Ammon (2 Sam. 10:6, 8).

places.name: Tower
places.summary: (Neh. 3:11; 12:38), a tower at the north-western angle of the second wall of Jerusalem.

places.name: Ulai
places.summary: The Eulaus of the Greeks; a river of Susiana. It was probably the eastern branch of the Choasper (Kerkhan), which divided into two branches some 20 miles above the city of Susa.

places.name: Uphaz
places.summary: Probably another name for Ophir (Jer. 10:9).

places.name: Uzza
places.summary: Strengh, a garden in which Manasseh and Amon were buried (2 Kings 21:18, 26). It was probably near the king’s palace in Jerusalem, or may have formed part of the palace grounds.

places.name: valley of Shaveh
places.summary: Valley of the plain the ancient name of the “king’s dale”, or Kidron, on the north side of Jerusalem (Gen. 14:17).

places.name: valley of Succoth
places.summary: A city on the east of Jordan, identified with Tell Dar’ala, a high mound, a mass of debris, in the plain north of Jabbok and about one mile from it (Josh. 13:27).

places.name: Zaanannim
places.summary: Wanderings; the unloading of tents, so called probably from the fact of nomads in tents encamping amid the cities and villages of that region, a place in the north-west of Lake Merom, near Kedesh, in Naphtali.

places.name: Zalmonah
places.summary: Shady, one of the stations of the Israelites in the wilderness (Num. 33:41, 42).

places.name: Zaphon
places.summary: ; now Qos

places.name: Zarethan
places.summary: When the Hebrews crossed the Jordan, as soon as the feet of the priests were dipped in the water, the flow of the stream was arrested. The point of arrest was the “city of Adam beside Zaretan,” probably near Succoth, at the mouth of the Jabbok, some 30 miles up the river from where the people were encamped.

places.name: Zedad
places.summary: Side; sloping place, a town in the north of Palestine, near Hamath (Num. 34:8; Ezek. 47:15).

places.name: Zela
places.summary: Slope; side, a town in Benjamin, where Saul and his son Jonathan were buried (2 Sam. 21:14).

places.name: Zered
places.summary: Zared, luxuriance; willow bush, a brook or valley communicating with the Dead Sea near its southern extremity (Num. 21:12; Deut. 2:14). It is called the “brook of the willows” (Isa. 15:7) and the “river of the wilderness” (Amos 6:14).

places.name: Zin
places.summary: A low palm-tree, the south-eastern corner of the desert et-Tih, the wilderness of Paran, between the Gulf of Akabah and the head of the Wady Guraiyeh (Num. 13:21).

places.name: Abana
places.summary: Stony (Heb. marg. “Amanah,” perennial), the chief river of Damascus (2 Kings 5:12). Its modern name is Barada, the Chrysorrhoas, or “golden stream,” of the Greeks.

places.name: Abel-keramim
places.summary: Heb. ‘abel (Judg. 11:33), a “grassy plain” or “meadow.”

places.name: Abel-mizraim
places.summary: Meadow of Egypt, or mourning of Egypt, a place “beyond,” i.e., on the west of Jordan, at the “threshing-floor of Atad.” Here the Egyptians mourned seventy days for Jacob (Gen. 50:4-11).

places.name: Abel-shittim
places.summary: Meadow of the acacias, frequently called simply “Shittim” (Num. 25:1; Josh. 2:1; Micah 6:5), a place on the east of Jordan, in the plain of Moab, nearly opposite Jericho.

places.name: Abilene
places.summary: A plain, a district lying on the east slope of the Anti-Lebanon range; so called from its chief town, Abila (Luke 3:1), which stood in the Suk Wady Barada, between Heliopolis (Baalbec) and Damascus, 38 miles from the former and 18 from the latter.

places.name: Accad
places.summary: The high land or mountains, a city in the land of Shinar. It has been identified with the mounds of Akker Kuf, some 50 miles to the north of Babylon; but this is doubtful.

places.name: Acco
places.summary: Sultry or sandy, a town and harbour of Phoenicia, in the tribe of Asher, but never acquired by them (Judg. 1:31). It was known to the ancient Greeks and Romans by the name of Ptolemais, from Ptolemy the king of Egypt, who rebuilt it about B.C. 100.

places.name: Adam
places.summary: Is referred to in Josh. 3:16. It stood “beside Zarethan,” on the west bank of Jordan (1 Kings 4:12).

places.name: Adamah
places.summary: Red earth, a fortified city of Naphtali, probably the modern Damieh, on the west side of the sea of Tiberias (Josh. 19:33, 36).

places.name: Adami-nekeb
places.summary: Cavern, a town on the boundary of Naphtali (Josh. 19:33).

places.name: Adar
places.summary: Large, the sixth month of the civil and the twelfth of the ecclesiastical year of the Jews (Esther 3:7, 13; 8:12; 9:1, 15, 17, 19, 21). It included the days extending from the new moon of our March to the new moon of April.

places.name: Addon
places.summary: Low, one of the persons named in Neh. 7:61 who could not “shew their father’s house” on the return from captivity.

places.name: Adramyttium
places.summary: A city of Asia Minor on the coast of Mysia, which in early times was called AEolis. The ship in which Paul embarked at Caesarea belonged to this city (Acts 27:2).

places.name: Adria
places.summary: (Acts 27:27; R.V., “the sea of Adria”), the Adriatic Sea, including in Paul’s time the whole of the Mediterranean lying between Crete and Sicily.

places.name: Aenon
places.summary: Springs, a place near Salim where John baptized (John 3:23). It was probably near the upper source of the Wady Far’ah, an open valley extending from Mount Ebal to the Jordan.

places.name: Ahlab
places.summary: Fatness, a town of Asher lying within the unconquered Phoenician border (Judg. 1:31), north-west of the Sea of Galilee; commonly identified with Giscala, now el-Jish.

places.name: Ai
places.summary: A city in the Ammonite territory (Jer. 49:3).

places.name: Alemeth
places.summary: A sacerdotal city of Benjamin (1 Chr. 6:60), called also Almon (Josh. 21:18), now Almit, a mile north-east of the ancient Anathoth.

places.name: Allon-bacuth
places.summary: Oak of weeping, a tree near Bethel, at the spot where Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, was buried (Gen. 35:8). Large trees, from their rarity in the plains of Palestine, were frequently designated as landmarks.

places.name: Almon
places.summary: Hidden, one of the sacerdotal cities of Benjamin (Josh. 21:18), called also Alemeth (1 Chr. 6:60).

places.name: Amana
places.summary: A mountain (Cant. 4:8), probably the southern summit of Anti-Libanus, at the base of which are the sources of the Abana.

places.name: Ammah
places.summary: A cubit, the name of a hill which Joab and Abishai reached as the sun went down, when they were in pursuit of Abner (2 Sam. 2:24).

places.name: Amphipolis
places.summary: City on both sides, a Macedonian city, a great Roman military station, through which Paul and Silas passed on their way from Philippi to Thessalonica, a distance of 33 Roman miles from Philippi (Acts 17:1).

places.name: Ananiah
places.summary: Protected by Jehovah, the name of a town in the tribe of Benjamin between Nob and Hazor (Neh. 11:32).

places.name: Anem
places.summary: Two fountains, a Levitical city in the tribe of Issachar (1 Chr. 6:73).

places.name: Aner
places.summary: A city of Manasseh given to the Levites of Kohath’s family (1 Chr. 6:70).

places.name: Anim
places.summary: Fountains, a city in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:50), now el-Ghuwein, near Eshtemoh, about 10 miles south-west of Hebron.

places.name: Antipatris
places.summary: A city built by Herod the Great, and called by this name in honour of his father, Antipater. It lay between Caesarea and Lydda, two miles inland, on the great Roman road from Caesarea to Jerusalem.

places.name: Aphik
places.summary: (Judg. 1:31); Aphek (Josh. 13:4; 19:30), stronghold.

places.name: Apollonia
places.summary: A city of Macedonia between Amphipolis and Thessalonica, from which it was distant about 36 miles.

places.name: Appii forum
places.summary: I.e., “the market of Appius” (Acts 28:15, R.V.), a town on the road, the “Appian Way,” from Rome to Brundusium. It was 43 miles from Rome. Here Paul was met by some Roman Christians on his way to the capital.

places.name: Arab
places.summary: Ambush, a city in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:52), now Er-Rabiyeh.

places.name: Arabah
places.summary: Plain, in the Revised Version of 2 Kings 14:25; Josh. 3:16; 8:14; 2 Sam. 2:29; 4:7 (in all these passages the A.V. has “plain”); Amos 6:14 (A.V. “wilderness”).

places.name: Armageddon
places.summary: Occurs only in Rev. 16:16 (R.V., “Har-Magedon”), as symbolically designating the place where the “battle of that great day of God Almighty” (ver. 14) shall be fought.

places.name: Aroer
places.summary: A city in the south of Judah, 12 miles south-east of Beersheba, to which David sent presents after recovering the spoil from the Amalekites at Ziklag (1 Sam. 30:26, 28).

places.name: Ashkenaz
places.summary: One of the three sons of Gomer (Gen. 10:3), and founder of one of the tribes of the Japhetic race.

places.name: Ashteroth-karnaim
places.summary: Ashteroth of the two horns, the abode of the Rephaim (Gen. 14:5). It may be identified with Ashtaroth preceding; called “Karnaim”, i.e., the “two-horned” (the crescent moon).

places.name: Atroth-shophan
places.summary: Hidden, or hollow, a town east of Jordan (Num. 32:35), built by the children of Gad.

places.name: Avva
places.summary: A place in Assyria from which colonies were brought to Samaria (2 Kings 17:24). It is probably the same with Ivah (18:34; 19:13; Isa. 37:13).

places.name: Azal
places.summary: (Zech. 14:5) should perhaps be rendered “very near” = “the way of escape shall be made easy.”

places.name: Azotus
places.summary: The Grecized form (Acts 8:40, etc.) of Ashdod.

places.name: Baal
places.summary: The name of a place inhabited by the Simeonites, the same probably as Baal-ath-beer (1 Chr. 4:33; Josh. 19:8).

places.name: Baal-hamon
places.summary: Place of a multitude, a place where Solomon had an extensive vineyard (Cant. 8:11). It has been supposed to be identical with Baal-gad, and also with Hammon in the tribe of Asher (Josh. 19:28).

places.name: Baal-hazor
places.summary: Having a courtyard, or Baal’s village, the place on the borders of Ephraim and Benjamin where Absalom held the feast of sheep-shearing when Amnon was assassinated (2 Sam. 13:23).

places.name: Baal-hermon
places.summary: A city near Mount Hermon inhabited by the Ephraimites (1 Chr. 5:23).

places.name: Baal-shalishah
places.summary: Lord of Shalisha, a place from which a man came with provisions for Elisha, apparently not far from Gilgal (2 Kings 4:42).

places.name: Baal-tamar
places.summary: Lord of palm trees, a place in the tribe of Benjamin near Gibeah of Saul (Judg. 20:33). It was one of the sanctuaries or groves of Baal.

places.name: Baalah
places.summary: A city in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:29), elsewhere called Balah (Josh. 19:3) and Bilhah (1 Chr. 4:29).

places.name: Baalath
places.summary: A town of the tribe of Dan (Josh. 19:44). It was fortified by Solomon (1 Kings 9:18; 2 Chr. 8:6).

places.name: Baalath-beer
places.summary: Baalah of the well, (Josh. 19:8, probably the same as Baal, mentioned in 1 Chr. 4:33, a city of Simeon.

places.name: Baale-judah
places.summary: Lords of Judah, a city in the tribe of Judah from which David brought the ark into Jerusalem (2 Sam. 6:2).

places.name: Balah
places.summary: A city in the tribe of Simeon (Josh. 19:3), elsewhere called Bilhah (1 Chr. 4:29) and Baalah (Josh. 15:29).

places.name: Bamah
places.summary: A height, a name used simply to denote a high place where the Jews worshipped idols (Ezek. 20:29).

places.name: Bath-rabbim
places.summary: Daughter of many, the name of one of the gates of the city of Heshbon, near which were pools (Cant. 7:4).

places.name: Bealoth
places.summary: Citizens, a town in the extreme south of Judah (Josh. 15:24); probably the same as Baalath-beer (19:8).

places.name: Bealoth
places.summary: Citizens, a town in the extreme south of Judah (Josh. 15:24); probably the same as Baalath-beer (19:8).

places.name: Beer
places.summary: A place where a well was dug by the direction of Moses, at the forty-fourth station of the Hebrews in their wanderings (Num. 21:16-18) in the wilderness of Moab.

places.name: Beer
places.summary: A town in the tribe of Judah to which Jotham fled for fear of Abimelech (Judg. 9:21).

places.name: Beer-elim
places.summary: Well of heroes, probably the name given to Beer, the place where the chiefs of Israel dug a well (Num. 21:16; Isa. 15:8).

places.name: Bene-berak
places.summary: uk.geocities.com/jonpartin/joshua4.html

places.name: Bered
places.summary: A town in the south of Palestine (Gen. 16:14), in the desert of Shur, near Lahai-roi.

places.name: Betah
places.summary: Confidence, a city belonging to Hadadezer, king of Zobah, which yielded much spoil of brass to David (2 Sam. 8:8).

places.name: Beth-anoth
places.summary: House of answers, a city in the mountainous district of Judah (Josh. 15:59).

places.name: Beth-arbel
places.summary: House of God’s court, a place alluded to by Hosea (10:14) as the scene of some great military exploit, but not otherwise mentioned in Scripture.

places.name: Beth-barah
places.summary: House of crossing, a place south of the scene of Gideon’s victory (Judg. 7:24). It was probably the chief ford of the Jordan in that district, and may have been that by which Jacob crossed when he returned from Mesopotamia, near the Jabbok (Gen. 32:22), and at which Jephthah slew the Ephraimites (Judg. 12:4).

places.name: Beth-car
places.summary: Sheep-house, a place to which the Israelites pursued the Philistines west from Mizpeh (1 Sam. 7:11).

places.name: Beth-dagon
places.summary: A city in the low country or plain of Judah, near Philistia (Josh. 15:41); the modern Beit Degan, about 5 miles from Lydda.

places.name: Beth-dagon
places.summary: A city near the south-east border of Asher (Josh. 19:27). It was a Philistine colony.

places.name: Beth-diblathaim
places.summary: House of two cakes of figs, a city of Moab, upon which Jeremiah (48:22) denounced destruction. It is called also Almon-diblathaim (Num. 33:46) and Diblath (Ezek. 6:14).

places.name: Beth-gamul
places.summary: Camel-house, a city in the “plain country” of Moab denounced by the prophet (Jer. 48:23); probably the modern Um-el-Jemal, near Bozrah, one of the deserted cities of the Hauran.

places.name: Beth-gilgal
places.summary: House of Gilgal, a place from which the inhabitants gathered for the purpose of celebrating the rebuilding of the walls on the return exile (Neh. 12:29).

places.name: Beth-horon
places.summary: House of the hollow, or of the cavern, the name of two towns or villages (2 Chr. 8:5; 1 Chr. 7:24) in the territory of Ephraim, on the way from Jerusalem to Joppa.

places.name: Beth-le-aphrah
places.summary: (R.V. Micah 1:10), house of dust. The Authorized Version reads “in the house of Aphrah.”

places.name: Beth-shemesh
places.summary: A city between Dothan and the Jordan, near the southern border of Issachar (Josh. 19:22), 7 1/2 miles south of Beth-shean.

places.name: Beth-tappuah
places.summary: House of apples, a town of Judah, now Tuffuh, 5 miles west of Hebron (Josh. 15:53).

places.name: Bethany
places.summary: The Revised Version in John 1:28 has this word instead of Bethabara, on the authority of the oldest manuscripts.

places.name: Bethesda
places.summary: House of mercy, a reservoir (Gr. kolumbethra, “a swimming bath”) with five porches, close to the sheep-gate or market (Neh. 3:1; John 5:2). Eusebius the historian (A.D. 330) calls it “the sheep-pool.”

places.name: Bethlehem
places.summary: A city of Zebulun, mentioned only in Josh. 19:15.

places.name: Bethlehem Ephrathah
places.summary: The ancient name of Bethlehem in Judah (Gen. 35:16, 19; 48:7). In Ruth 1:2 it is called “Bethlehem-Judah,” but the inhabitants are called “Ephrathites;” in Micah 5:2, “Bethlehem-Ephratah;” in Matt. 2:6, “Bethlehem in the land of Judah.”

places.name: Bethuel
places.summary: A southern city of Judah (1 Chr. 4:30); called also Bethul (Josh. 19:4) and Bethel (12:16; 1 Sam. 30:27).

places.name: Bezek
places.summary: The place where Saul numbered the forces of Israel and Judah (1 Sam. 11:8); somewhere in the centre of the country, near the Jordan valley.

places.name: Bilhah
places.summary: Faltering; bashful, Rachel’s handmaid, whom she gave to Jacob (Gen. 29:29). She was the mother of Dan and Naphtali (Gen. 30:3-8). Reuben was cursed by his father for committing adultry with her (35:22; 49:4).

places.name: Bor-ashan
places.summary: Smoking furnace, one of the places where “David himself and his men were wont to haunt” (1 Sam. 30:30, 31). It is probably identical with Ashan (Josh. 15:42; 19:7), a Simeonite city in the Negeb, i.e., the south, belonging to Judah.

places.name: Bozrah
places.summary: A Moabite city in the “plain country” (Jer. 48:24), i.e., on the high level down on the east of the Dead Sea.

places.name: Buz
places.summary: A district in Arabia Petrea (Jer. 25:23).

places.name: Cabul
places.summary: A town on the eastern border of Asher (Josh. 19:27), probably one of the towns given by Solomon to Hiram; the modern Kabul, some 8 miles east of Accho, on the very borders of Galilee.

places.name: Cabul
places.summary: A district in the north-west of Galilee, near to Tyre, containing twenty cities given to Hiram by Solomon as a reward for various services rendered to him in building the temple (1 Kings 9:13), and as payment of the six score talents of gold he had borrowed from him.

places.name: Caleb-ephratah
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1277 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Canneh
places.summary: Mentioned only in Ezek. 27:23.

places.name: Casiphia
places.summary: Silver, a place between Babylon and Jerusalem, where Iddo resided (Ezra 8:17); otherwise unknown.

places.name: Chephar-haammoni
places.summary: ; now Khirbat Kafr Ana

places.name: Chesalon
places.summary: Strength; confidence, a place on the border of Judah, on the side of Mount Jearim (Josh. 15:10); probably identified with the modern village of Kesla, on the western mountains of Judah.

places.name: Chesil
places.summary: Ungodly, a town in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:30); probably the same as Bethul (19:4) and Bethuel (1 Chr. 4:30); now Khelasa.

places.name: Chesulloth
places.summary: Fertile places; the loins, a town of Issachar, on the slopes of some mountain between Jezreel and Shunem (Josh. 19:18).

places.name: Chezib
places.summary: Deceitful, a town where Shelah, the son of Judah, was born (Gen. 38:5).

places.name: Chilmad
places.summary: A place or country unknown which, along with Sheba and Asshur, traded with Tyre (Ezek. 27:23).

places.name: Chinnereth
places.summary: Lyre, the singular form of the word (Deut. 3:17; Josh. 19:35), which is also used in the plural form, Chinneroth, the name of a fenced city which stood near the shore of the lake of Galilee, a little to the south of Tiberias.

places.name: Chinnereth
places.summary: Lyre, the singular form of the word (Deut. 3:17; Josh. 19:35), which is also used in the plural form, Chinneroth, the name of a fenced city which stood near the shore of the lake of Galilee, a little to the south of Tiberias.

places.name: Chios
places.summary: Mentioned in Acts 20:15, an island in the Aegean Sea, about 5 miles distant from the mainland, having a roadstead, in the shelter of which Paul and his companions anchored for a night when on his third missionary return journey.

places.name: Chitlish
places.summary: A man’s wall, a town in the plain of Judah (Josh. 15:40).

places.name: Clauda
places.summary: A small island off the southwest coast of Crete, passed by Paul on his voyage to Rome (Acts 27:16). It is about 7 miles long and 3 broad.

places.name: Cnidus
places.summary: A town and harbour on the extreme south-west of the peninsula of Doris in Asia Minor.

places.name: Colossae
places.summary: Or Colosse, a city of Phrygia, on the Lycus, which is a tributary of the Maeander. It was about 12 miles above Laodicea, and near the great road from Ephesus to the Euphrates, and was consequently of some mercantile importance.

places.name: Coos
places.summary: (written Cos in the R.V.), a small island, one of the Sporades in the Aegean Sea, in the north-west of Rhodes, off the coast of Caria. Paul on his return from his third missionary journey, passed the night here after sailing from Miletus (Acts 21:1).

places.name: Cozeba
places.summary: (1 Chr. 4:22), the same as Chezib and Achzib, a place in the lowlands of Judah (Gen. 38:5; Josh. 15:44).

places.name: Cun
places.summary: One of the cities of Hadarezer, king of Syria. David procured brass (i.e., bronze or copper) from it for the temple (1 Chr. 18:8).

places.name: Cushan
places.summary: Probably a poetic or prolonged name of the land of Cush, the Arabian Cush (Hab. 3:7). Some have, however, supposed this to be the same as Chushan-rishathaim (Judg. 3:8, 10), i.e., taking the latter part of the name as a title or local appellation, Chushan “of the two iniquities” (= oppressing Israel, and provoking them to idolatry), a Mesopotamian king, identified by Rawlinson with Asshur-ris-ilim (the father of Tiglathpileser I.); but incorrectly, for the empire of Assyria…

places.name: Cuth
places.summary: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kutha

places.name: Cuthah
places.summary: One of the Babylonian cities or districts from which Shalmaneser transplanted certain colonists to Samaria (2 Kings 17:24). Some have conjectured that the “Cutheans” were identical with the “Cossaeans” who inhabited the hill-country to the north of the river Choaspes.

places.name: Dalmanutha
places.summary: A place on the west of the Sea of Galilee, mentioned only in Mark 8:10. In the parallel passage it is said that Christ came “into the borders of Magdala” (Matt. 15:39).

places.name: Dalmatia
places.summary: A mountainous country on the eastern shore of the Adriatic, a part of the Roman province of Illyricum. It still bears its ancient name. During Paul’s second imprisonment at Rome, Titus left him to visit Dalmatia (2 Tim. 4:10) for some unknown purpose.

places.name: Dannah
places.summary: Murmuring, a city (Josh. 15:49) in the mountains of Judah about 8 miles south-west of Hebron.

places.name: Debir
places.summary: A place near the “valley of Achor” (Josh. 15:7), on the north boundary of Judah, between Jerusalem and Jericho.

places.name: Destruction
places.summary: (Isa. 19:18; Heb. Ir-ha-Heres, “city of overthrow,” because of the evidence it would present of the overthrow of heathenism), the ideal title of On or Heliopolis.

places.name: Dibon
places.summary: A city of the tribe of Judah, inhabited after the Captivity (Neh. 11:25); called also Dimonah (Josh. 15:22).

places.name: Dimnah
places.summary: Dunghill, a city of Zebulun given to the Merarite Levites (Josh. 21:35).

places.name: Diviners' Oak
places.summary: (Judg. 9:37; A.V., “the plain of Meonenim;” R.V., “the oak of Meonenim”) means properly “soothsayers” or “sorcerers,” “wizards” (Deut. 18:10, 14; 2 Kings 21:6; Micah 5:12).

places.name: Dizahab
places.summary: Region of gold, a place in the desert of Sinai, on the western shore of the Elanitic gulf (Deut. 1:1).

places.name: Dragon Spring
places.summary: (Neh. 2:13), supposed by some to be identical with the Pool of Gihon.

places.name: Dura
places.summary: The circle, the plain near Babylon in which Nebuchadnezzar set up a golden image, mentioned in Dan. 3:1. The place still retains its ancient name.

places.name: east gate
places.summary: (Jer. 19:2), properly the Potter’s gate, the gate which led to the potter’s field, in the valley of Hinnom.

places.name: Ebez
places.summary: Tin, or white, a town in the tribe of Issachar (Josh. 19:20), at the north of the plain of Esdraelon.

places.name: Ebron
places.summary: A town in the north border of Asher (Josh. 19:28).

places.name: Ecbatana
places.summary: (Ezra 6:2), called Ecbatana by classical writers, the capital of northern Media. Here was the palace which was the residence of the old Median monarchs, and of Cyrus and Cambyses.

places.name: Eder
places.summary: Tower of the flock, a tower between Bethlehem and Hebron, near which Jacob first halted after leaving Bethlehem (Gen. 35:21).

places.name: Eder
places.summary: A city in the south of Judah, on the border of Idumea (Josh. 15:21).

places.name: Edrei
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1261 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Eglaim
places.summary: Two ponds, (Isa. 15:8), probably En-eglaim of Ezek. 47:10.

places.name: Egyptian Sea
places.summary: water

places.name: El-bethel
places.summary: God of Bethel, the name of the place where Jacob had the vision of the ladder, and where he erected an altar (Gen. 31:13; 35:7).

places.name: El-elohe-Israel
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-0390 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Elishah
places.summary: The oldest of the four sons of Javan (Gen. 10:4), whose descendants peopled Greece. It has been supposed that Elishah’s descendants peopled the Peloponnesus, which was known by the name of Elis.

places.name: Elkosh
places.summary: God my bow, the birth-place of Nahum the prophet (Nah. 1:1).

places.name: Elteke
places.summary: God is its fear, a city in the tribe of Dan. It was a city of refuge and a Levitical city (Josh. 21:23).

places.name: Eltekeh
places.summary: God is its fear, a city in the tribe of Dan. It was a city of refuge and a Levitical city (Josh. 21:23).

places.name: Eltekon
places.summary: from tyndale

places.name: Emek-keziz
places.summary: Abrupt; cut off, a city of the tribe of Benjamin (Josh. 18:21).

places.name: Emmaus
places.summary: Hot baths, a village “three-score furlongs” from jerusalem, where our Lord had an interview with two of his disciples on the day of his resurrection (Luke 24:13).

places.name: En-gannim
places.summary: A town in the plains of Judah (Josh. 15:34), north-west of Jerusalem, between Zanoah and Tappuah.

places.name: En-hakkore
places.summary: Fountain of the crier, the name of the spring in Lehi which burst forth in answer to Samson’s prayer when he was exhausted with the slaughter of the Philistines (Judg. 15:19).

places.name: En-tappuah
places.summary: En-tappuah, the well of the apple, probably one of the springs near Yassuf (Josh. 17:7).

places.name: Ephes-dammim
places.summary: Boundary of blood, a place in the tribe of Judah where the Philistines encamped when David fought with Goliath (1 Sam. 17:1). It was probably so called as having been the scene of frequent sanguinary conflicts between Israel and the Philistines.

places.name: Esek
places.summary: Quarrel, a well which Isaac’s herdsmen dug in the valley of Gerar, and so called because the herdsmen of Gerar quarrelled with them for its possession (Gen. 26:20).

places.name: Eshan
places.summary: A place in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:52), supposed to be the ruin es-Simia, near Dumah, south of Hebron.

places.name: Etam
places.summary: A village of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:32). Into some cleft (“top,” A.V.,; R.V., “cleft”) of a rock here Samson retired after his slaughter of the Philistines (Judg. 15:8, 11).

places.name: Etam
places.summary: A city of Judah, fortified by Rehoboam (2 Chr. 11:6). It was near Bethlehem and Tekoah, and some distance apparently to the north of (1). It seems to have been in the district called Nephtoah (or Netophah), where were the sources of the water from which Solomon’s gardens and pleasure-grounds and pools, as well as Bethlehem and the temple, were supplied.

places.name: Fair Havens
places.summary: A harbour in the south of Crete, some 5 miles to the east of which was the town of Lasea (Acts 27:8). Here the ship of Alexandria in which Paul and his companions sailed was detained a considerable time waiting for a favourable wind.

places.name: Gabbatha
places.summary: Gab Baitha, i.e., “the ridge of the house” = “the temple-mound,” on a part of which the fortress of Antonia was built. This “temple-mound” was covered with a tesselated “pavement” (Gr. lithostroton, i.e., “stone-paved”).

places.name: Gamad
places.summary: (Ezek. 27:11) brave warriors; R.V. marg., “valorous men;” others interpret this word as meaning “short-swordsmen,” or “daring ones”, the name of a class of men who were defenders of the towers of Tyre.

places.name: Gareb
places.summary: A hill near Jerusalem (Jer. 31:39), probably the hill of lepers, and consequently a place outside the boundary of the city.

places.name: gate of the children of the people
Gath-rimmon
places.summary: Another city of the same name in Manasseh, west of the Jordan (Josh. 21:25), called also Bileam (1 Chr. 6:70).

places.name: Gebim
places.summary: Cisterns, (rendered “pits,” Jer. 14:3; “locusts,” Isa. 33:4), a small place north of Jerusalem, whose inhabitants fled at the approach of the Assyrian army (Isa. 10:31).

places.name: Geder
places.summary: A walled place, (Josh. 12:13), perhaps the same as Gederah or Gedor (15:58).

places.name: Gedor
places.summary: 1 Chr. 4:39, the Gederah of Josh. 15:36, or the well-known Gerar, as the LXX. read, where the patriarchs of old had sojourned and fed their flocks (Gen. 20:1, 14, 15; 26:1, 6, 14).

places.name: Geliloth
places.summary: Circles; regions, a place in the border of Benjamin (Josh. 18:17); called Gilgal in 15:7.

places.name: Geruth Chimham
places.summary: Pining, probably the youngest son of Barzillai the Gileadite (2 Sam. 19:37-40). The “habitation of Chimham” (Jer. 41:17) was probably an inn or khan, which is the proper meaning of the Hebrew geruth, rendered “habitation”, established in later times in his possession at Bethlehem, which David gave to him as a reward for his loyalty in accompanying him to Jerusalem after the defeat of Absalom (1 Kings 2:7).

places.name: Gihon
places.summary: One of the four rivers of Eden (Gen. 2:13). It has been identified with the Nile. Others regard it as the Oxus, or the Araxes, or the Ganges.

places.name: Gilo
places.summary: A name given to Hashem, an inhabitant of Gizoh, a place somewhere in the mountains of Judah (1 Chr. 11:34; 2 Sam. 23:32, 34).

places.name: Gimzo
places.summary: A place fertile in sycamores, a city in the plain of Judah, the villages of which were seized by the Philistines (2 Chr. 28:18).

places.name: Goah
places.summary: A lowing, a place near Jerusalem, mentioned only in Jer. 31:39.

places.name: Gog
places.summary: The name of the leader of the hostile party described in Ezek. 38, 39, as coming from the “north country” and assailing the people of Israel to their own destruction.

places.name: Gur
places.summary: A whelp, a place near Ibleam where Jehu’s servants overtook and mortally wounded king Ahaziah (2 Kings 9:27); an ascent from the plain of Jezreel.

places.name: Gurbaal
places.summary: Sojourn of Baal, a place in Arabia (2 Chr. 26:7) where there was probably a temple of Baal.

places.name: Hadad-rimmon
places.summary: (composed of the names of two Syrian idols), the name of a place in the valley of Megiddo. It is alluded to by the prophet Zechariah (12:11) in a proverbial expression derived from the lamentation for Josiah, who was mortally wounded near this place (2 Chr. 35:22-25).

places.name: Hadashah
places.summary: New, a city in the valley of Judah (Josh. 15:37).

places.name: Hadrach
places.summary: The name of a country (Zech. 9:1) which cannot be identified. Rawlinson would identify it with Edessa.

places.name: Haeleph
places.summary: now Lifta

places.name: Hahiroth
places.summary: from tyndale

places.name: Halhul
places.summary: Full of hollows, a town in the highlands of Judah (Josh. 15:58). It is now a small village of the same name, and is situated about 5 miles north-east of Hebron on the way to Jerusalem.

places.name: Ham
places.summary: Warm, hot, and hence the south; also an Egyptian word meaning “black”, the youngest son of Noah (Gen. 5:32; comp. 9:22, 24).

places.name: Hamath-zobah
places.summary: Fortress of Zobah, (2 Chr. 8:3) is supposed by some to be a different place from the foregoing; but this is quite uncertain.

places.name: Hammoth-dor
places.summary: Warm springs, a Levitical city of Naphtali (Josh. 21:32); probably Hammath in 19:35.

places.name: Hamonah
places.summary: Multitude, a name figuratively assigned to the place in which the slaughter and burial of the forces of Gog were to take place (Ezek. 39:16).

places.name: Hanes
places.summary: A place in Egypt mentioned only in Isa. 30:4 in connection with a reproof given to the Jews for trusting in Egypt.

places.name: Hara
places.summary: Mountainous land, a province of Assyria (1 Chr. 5:26), between the Tigris and the Euphrates, along the banks of the Khabur, to which some of the Israelite captives were carried.

places.name: Havilah
places.summary: A land mentioned in Gen. 2:11 rich in gold and bdellium and onyx stone. The question as to the locality of this region has given rise to a great diversity of opinion.

places.name: Hazar-addar
places.summary: Village of Addar, a place in the southern boundary of Palestine (Num. 34:4), in the desert to the west of Kadesh-barnea.

places.name: Hazar-gaddah
places.summary: Village of fortune, a city on the south border of Judah (Josh. 15:27), midway between the Mediterranean and the Dead Sea.

places.name: Hazar-susah
places.summary: Village of the horse, the same as Sansannah, one of Solomon’s “chariot cities” (Josh. 15:31; 2 Chr. 1:14), a depot in the south border of Judah.

places.name: Hazor
places.summary: A city in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:23).

places.name: Hazor-hadattah
places.summary: New Hazor, a city in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:25).

places.name: Helbah
places.summary: Fatness, a town of the tribe of Asher (Judg. 1:31), in the plain of Phoenicia.

places.name: Helbon
places.summary: Fat; i.e., “fertile”, (Ezek. 27: 18 only), a place whence wine was brought to the great market of Tyre.

places.name: Heleph
places.summary: Exchange, a city on the north border of Naphtali (Josh. 19:33).

places.name: Helkath-hazzurim
places.summary: Plot of the sharp blades, or the field of heroes, (2 Sam. 2:16). After the battle of Gilboa, so fatal to Saul and his house, David, as divinely directed, took up his residence in Hebron, and was there anointed king over Judah.

places.name: Hereth
places.summary: Thicket, a wood in the mountains of Judah where David hid when pursued by Saul (1 Sam. 22:5). It was possibly while he was here that the memorable incident narrated in 2 Sam. 23:14-17, 1 Chr. 11:16-19 occurred.

places.name: Heshmon
places.summary: Fatness, a town in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:27).

places.name: Hezron
places.summary: A plain in the south of Judah, west of Kadesh-barnea (Josh. 15:3).

places.name: Hierapolis
places.summary: Sacred city, a city of Phrygia, where was a Christian church under the care of Epaphras (Col. 4:12, 13). This church was founded at the same time as that of Colosse.

places.name: hill Mizar
places.summary: Smallness, a summit on the eastern ridge of Lebanon, near which David lay after escaping from Absalom (Ps. 42:6).

places.name: Hobah
places.summary: Hiding-place, a place to the north of Damascus, to which Abraham pursued Chedorlaomer and his confederates (Gen. 14:15).

places.name: Horem
places.summary: Consecrated, one of the fenced cities of Naphtali (Josh. 19:38).

places.name: Hosah
places.summary: A place on the border of the tribe of Asher (Josh. 19:29), a little to the south of Zidon.

places.name: Hukkok
places.summary: Decreed, a town near Zebulun, not far from Jordan, on the border of Naphtali (Josh. 19:34).

places.name: Hukok
places.summary: Decreed, a town near Zebulun, not far from Jordan, on the border of Naphtali (Josh. 19:34).

places.name: Idalah
places.summary: Snares(?), a city near the west border of Zebulun (Josh. 19:15).

places.name: Idumea
places.summary: The Greek form of Edom (Isa. 34:5, 6; Ezek. 35:15; 36:5, but in R.V. “Edom”).

places.name: Iim
places.summary: A city in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:29).

places.name: Illyricum
places.summary: A country to the north-west of Macedonia, on the eastern shores of the Adriatic, now almost wholly comprehended in Dalmatia, a name formerly given to the southern part of Illyricum (2 Tim. 4:10).

places.name: Ithlah
places.summary: Suspended; high, a city on the borders of Dan (Josh. 19:42).

places.name: Ituraea
places.summary: A district in the north-east of Palestine, forming, along with the adjacent territory of Trachonitis, the tetrarchy of Philip (Luke 3:1). The present Jedur comprehends the chief part of Ituraea.

places.name: Iyim
places.summary: One of the stations of the Israelites in the wilderness (Num. 33:45).

places.name: Jabez
places.summary: A place inhabited by several families of the scribes (1 Chr. 2:55).

places.name: Jabneel
places.summary: A town in the north boundary of Judah (Josh. 15:11), called afterwards by the Greeks Jamnia, the modern Yebna, 11 miles south of Jaffa.

places.name: Jabneel
places.summary: A town on the border of Naphtali (Josh. 19:33).

places.name: Jabneh
places.summary: Building, (2 Chr. 26:6), identical with Jabneel (Josh. 15:11).

places.name: Jagur
places.summary: Place of sojourn, a city on the southern border of Judah (Josh. 15:21).

places.name: Jair
places.summary: region

places.name: Janim
places.summary: Slumber, a town in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:53).

places.name: Janoah
places.summary: A town of Northern Palestine, within the boundaries of Naphtali.

places.name: Japhia
places.summary: A town in the southern boundary of Zebulum (Josh. 19:12); now Yafa, 2 miles south-west of Nazareth.

places.name: Jarmuth
places.summary: A Levitical city of the tribe of Issachar (Josh. 21:29), supposed by some to be the Ramah of Samuel (1 Sam. 19:22).

places.name: Jebusite
