places.summary: The name of the original inhabitants of Jebus, mentioned frequently among the seven nations doomed to destruction (Gen. 10:16; 15:21; Ex. 3:8, 17; 13:5, etc.).

places.name: Jegar-sahadutha
places.summary: Pile of testimony, the Aramaic or Syriac name which Laban gave to the pile of stones erected as a memorial of the covenant between him and Jacob (Gen. 31:47), who, however, called it in Hebrew by an equivalent name, Galeed.

places.name: Jehud
places.summary: now Yehud

places.name: Jeruel
places.summary: Founded by God, a “desert” on the ascent from the valley of the Dead Sea towards Jerusalem. It lay beyond the wilderness of Tekoa, in the direction of Engedi (2 Chr. 20:16, 20).

places.name: Jeshanah
places.summary: A city of the kingdom of Israel (2 Chr. 13:19).

places.name: Jeshua
places.summary: A city of Judah (Neh. 11:26).

places.name: Jetur
places.summary: An enclosure, one of the twelve sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15).

places.name: Jokdeam
places.summary: A city in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:56).

places.name: Jokmeam
places.summary: Gathering of the people, a city of Ephraim, which was given with its suburbs to the Levites (1 Chr. 6:68).

places.name: Jokmeam
places.summary: Gathering of the people, a city of Ephraim, which was given with its suburbs to the Levites (1 Chr. 6:68).

places.name: Jorkoam
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1283 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Judean
places.summary: After the Captivity this name was applied to the whole of the country west of the Jordan (Hag. 1:1, 14; 2:2).

places.name: Tahtimhodshi
places.summary: The land of the newly inhabited, (2 Sam. 24:6). It is conjectured that, instead of this word, the reading should be, “the Hittites of Kadesh,” the Hittite capital, on the Orontes.

places.name: Kamon
places.summary: Full of stalks, a place (Judg. 10:5) where Jair was buried. It has usually been supposed to have been a city of Gilead, on the east of Jordan.

places.name: Kanah
places.summary: A town in the north of Asher (Josh. 19:28). It has been identified with ‘Ain-Kana, a village on the brow of a valley some 7 miles south-east of Tyre.

places.name: Karka
places.summary: A floor; bottom, a place between Adar and Azmon, about midway between the Mediterranean and the Dead Sea (Josh. 15:3).

places.name: Karkor
places.summary: Foundation, a place in the open desert wastes on the east of Jordan (Judg. 8:10), not far beyond Succoth and Penuel, to the south.

places.name: Kartah
places.summary: City, a town in the tribe of Zebulun assigned to the Levites of the family of Merari (Josh. 21:34).

places.name: Kartan
places.summary: Double city, a town of Naphali, assigned to the Gershonite Levites, and one of the cities of refuge (Josh. 21:32).

places.name: Kattath
places.summary: (Josh. 19:15), a town of Asher, has been identified with Kana el Jelil.

places.name: Kedesh
places.summary: A city of Issachar (1 Chr. 6:72).

places.name: Kerioth-hezron
places.summary: A town in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:25). Judas the traitor was probably a native of this place, and hence his name Iscariot.

places.name: Kibzaim
places.summary: Two heaps, a city of Ephraim, assigned to the Kohathite Levites, and appointed as a city of refuge (Josh. 21: 22).

places.name: Kinah
places.summary: An elegy, a city in the extreme south of Judah (Josh. 15:22).

places.name: Kiriathaim
places.summary: A city of refuge in Naphtali (1 Chr. 6:76).

places.name: Kitron
places.summary: Knotty, a city of Zebulun (Judg. 1:30), called also Kattath (Josh. 19:15); supposed to be “Cana of Galilee.”

places.name: Koa
places.summary: He-camel, occurs only in Ezek. 23:23, some province or place in the Babylonian empire, used in this passage along with Shoa.

places.name: Laban
places.summary: A city in the Arabian desert in the route of the Israelites (Deut. 1:1), probably identical with Libnah (Num. 33:20).

places.name: Laishah
places.summary: A place mentioned in Isa. 10:30.

places.name: Lasea
places.summary: A city in the island of Crete (Acts 27:8).

places.name: Lasha
places.summary: Fissure, a place apparently east of the Dead Sea (Gen. 10:19).

places.name: Lasharon
places.summary: now Sharona

places.name: Lebonah
places.summary: Frankincense, a town near Shiloh, on the north side of Bethel (Judg. 21:19).

places.name: Luz
places.summary: A place in the land of the Hittites, founded (Judg. 1:26) by “a man who came forth out of the city of Luz.”

places.name: Lycaonia
places.summary: An inland province of Asia Minor, on the west of Cappadocia and the south of Galatia. It was a Roman province, and its chief towns were Iconium, Lystra, and Derbe.

places.name: Lycia
places.summary: A wolf, a province in the south-west of Asia Minor, opposite the island of Rhodes. It forms part of the region now called Tekeh. It was a province of the Roman empire when visited by Paul (Acts 21:1; 27:5).

places.name: Maarath
places.summary: Desolation, a place in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:59), probably the modern village Beit Ummar, 6 miles north of Hebron.

places.name: Machbenah
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1281 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Madmen
places.summary: Ibid., a Moabite town threatened with the sword of the Babylonians (Jer. 48:2).

places.name: Madmenah
places.summary: Ibid., a town in Benjamin, not far from Jerusalem, towards the north (Isa. 10:31). The same Hebrew word occurs in Isa. 25:10, where it is rendered “dunghill.”

places.name: Magadan
places.summary: A tower, a town in Galilee, mentioned only in Matt. 15:39. In the parallel passage in Mark 8:10 this place is called Dalmanutha. It was the birthplace of Mary called the Magdalen, or Mary Magdalene.

places.name: Manahath
places.summary: now Malha

places.name: Mareal
places.summary: Trembling, a place on the southern boundary of Zebulun (Josh. 19:11).

places.name: Maroth
places.summary: Bitterness; i.e., “perfect grief”, a place not far from Jerusalem; mentioned in connection with the invasion of the Assyrian army (Micah 1:12).

places.name: Mashal
places.summary: Entreaty, a levitical town in the tribe of Asher (1 Chr. 6:74); called Mishal (Josh. 21:30).

places.name: Me-jarkon
places.summary: Waters of yellowness, or clear waters, a river in the tribe of Dan (Josh. 19:46).

places.name: Mearah
places.summary: A cave, a place in the northern boundary of Palestine (Josh. 13:4).

places.name: Meconah
places.summary: A base or foundation, a town in the south of Judah (Neh. 11:28), near Ziklag.

places.name: Melita
places.summary: (Acts 27:28), an island in the Mediterranean, the modern Malta. Here the ship in which Paul was being conveyed a prisoner to Rome was wrecked.

places.name: Merathaim
places.summary: Double rebellion, probably a symbolical name given to Babylon (Jer. 50:21), denoting rebellion exceeding that of other nations.

places.name: Meroz
places.summary: A plain in the north of Palestine, the inhabitants of which were severely condemned because they came not to help Barak against Sisera (Judg. 5:23: comp. 21:8-10; 1 Sam. 11:7).

places.name: Mesha
places.summary: A plain in that part of the boundaries of Arabia inhabited by the descendants of Joktan (Gen. 10:30).

places.name: Metheg-ammah
places.summary: Bridle of the mother, a figurative name for a chief city, as in 2 Sam. 8:1, “David took Metheg-ammah out of the hand of the Philistines” (R.V., “took the bridle of the mother-city”); i.e., subdued their capital or strongest city, viz., Gath (1 Chr. 18:1).

places.name: Middin
places.summary: Measures, one of the six cities “in the wilderness,” on the west of the Dead Sea, mentioned along with En-gedi (Josh. 15:61).

places.name: Migdal-el
places.summary: Tower of God, a fortified city of Naphtali (Josh. 19:38), supposed by some to be identical with Magdala.

places.name: Migdal-gad
places.summary: Tower of fortune, a town in the plains of Judah, probably the modern el-Mejdel, a little to the north-east of Ascalon (Josh. 15:37).

places.name: Minni
places.summary: Only in Jer. 51:27, as the name of a province in Armenia, which was at this time under the Median kings.

places.name: Misgab
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1274 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Mitylene
places.summary: The chief city of the island of Lesbos, on its east coast, in the AEgean Sea. Paul, during his third missionary journey, touched at this place on his way from Corinth to Judea (Acts 20:14), and here tarried for a night.

places.name: Mizpah
places.summary: Another place in Gilead, at the foot of Mount Hermon, inhabited by Hivites (Josh. 11:3, 8). The name in Hebrew here has the article before it, “the Mizpeh,” “the watch-tower.”

places.name: Mizpeh
places.summary: A town of Moab to which David removed his parents for safety during his persecution by Saul (1 Sam. 22:3). This was probably the citadel known as Kir-Moab, now Kerak.

places.name: Moreh
places.summary: Probably identical with “little Hermon,” the modern Jebel ed-Duhy, or perhaps one of the lower spurs of this mountain.

places.name: Moresheth-gath
places.summary: Possession of the wine-press, the birthplace of the prophet Micah (1:14), who is called the “Morasthite” (Jer. 26:18).

places.name: Moriah
places.summary: The chosen of Jehovah. Some contend that Mount Gerizim is meant, but most probably we are to regard this as one of the hills of Jerusalem. Here Solomon’s temple was built, on the spot that had been the threshing-floor of Ornan the Jebusite (2 Sam. 24:24, 25; 2 Chr. 3:1).

places.name: Mortar
places.summary: Mortar, a place in or near Jerusalem inhabited by silver merchants (Zeph. 1:11).

places.name: Moserah
places.summary: A bond, one of the stations of the Israelites in the wilderness (Deut. 10:6), at the foot of Mount Hor. (Comp. Num. 33:37, 38).

places.name: most holy
places.summary: mobile

places.name: most holy place
places.summary: mobile

places.name: mount Baalah
places.summary: A mountain on the north-western boundary of Judah and Dan (Josh. 15:11).

places.name: mount Ephron
places.summary: A mountain range which formed one of the landmarks on the north boundary of the tribe of Judah (Josh. 15:9), probably the range on the west side of the Wady Beit-Hanina.

places.name: mount Heres
places.summary: “Mount Heres” (Judg. 1:35), Heb. Har-heres, i.e., “sun-mountain;” probably identical with Irshemesh in Josh. 19:41.

places.name: mount Jearim
places.summary: Forests, a mountain on the border of Judah (Josh. 15:10).

places.name: mount of Olives
places.summary: So called from the olive trees with which its sides are clothed, is a mountain ridge on the east of Jerusalem (1 Kings 11:7; Ezek. 11:23; Zech. 14:4), from which it is separated by the valley of Kidron.

places.name: mount Perazim
places.summary: Mount of breaches, only in Isa. 28:21.

places.name: mount Seir
places.summary: A mountain range (not the Edomite range, Gen. 32:3) lying between the Wady Aly and the Wady Ghurab (Josh. 15:10).

places.name: mount Sion
places.summary: Denotes Mount Hermon in Deut. 4:48; called Sirion by the Sidonians, and by the Amorites Shenir (Deut. 3:9).

places.name: mount Zalmon
places.summary: Shady; or Zalmon, a hill covered with dark forests, south of Shechem, from which Abimelech and his men gathered wood to burn that city (Judg. 9:48).

places.name: mount Zemaraim
places.summary: A mount in the highlands of Ephraim, to the north of Jerusalem (2 Chr. 13:4-20).

places.name: Mozah
places.summary: An issuing of water, a city of Benjamin (Josh. 18:26).

places.name: Myra
places.summary: One of the chief towns of Lycia, in Asia Minor, about 2 1/2 miles from the coast (Acts 27:5).

places.name: Naamah
places.summary: A city in the plain of Judah (Josh. 15:41), supposed by some to be identified with Na’aneh, some 5 miles south-east of Makkedah.

places.name: Naarah
places.summary: Girl, a town on the boundary between Ephraim and Benjamin (Josh. 16:7), not far probably from Jericho, to the north (1 Chr. 7:28).

places.name: Naaran
places.summary: Boyish, juvenile, a town in Ephraim between Bethel and Jericho (1 Chr. 7:28).

places.name: Nahaliel
places.summary: Possession, or valley of God, one of the encampments of the Israelites in the wilderness (Num. 21:19), on the confines of Moab.

places.name: Nain
places.summary: (from Heb. nain, “green pastures,” “lovely”), the name of a town near the gate of which Jesus raised to life a widow’s son (Luke 7:11-17). It is identified with the village called Nein, standing on the north-western slope of Jebel ed-Duhy (=the “hill Moreh” = “Little hermon”), about 4 miles from Tabor and 25 southwest of Capernaum.

places.name: Naphish
places.summary: Refresher, one of the sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15; 1 Chr. 1:31).

places.name: Neah
places.summary: Shaking, or settlement, or descent, a town on the east side of Zebulun, not far from Rimmon (Josh. 19:13).

places.name: Neapolis
places.summary: New city, a town in Thrace at which Paul first landed in Europe (Acts 16:11). It was the sea-port of the inland town of Philippi, which was distant about 10 miles.

places.name: Nebaioth
places.summary: (Nabateans Petra)

places.name: Neballat
places.summary: Wickedness in secret, (Neh. 11:34), probably the village of Beit Nebala, about 4 miles north of Lydda.

places.name: Neiel
places.summary: Dwelling-place of God, a town in the territory of Asher, near its southern border (Josh. 19:27).

places.name: Nezib
places.summary: A town in the “plain” of Judah.

places.name: Nibshan
places.summary: Fertile; light soil, a city somewhere “in the wilderness” of Judah (Josh. 15:62), probably near Engedi.

places.name: Nicopolis
places.summary: City of victory, where Paul intended to winter (Titus 3:12). There were several cities of this name. The one here referred to was most probably that in Epirus, which was built by Augustus Caesar to commemorate his victory at the battle of Actium (B.C. 31).

places.name: Nimrah
places.summary: Pure, a city on the east of Jordan (Num. 32:3); probably the same as Beth-nimrah (Josh. 13:27).

places.name: Nimrod
places.summary: Firm, a descendant of Cush, the son of Ham. He was the first who claimed to be a “mighty one in the earth.” Babel was the beginning of his kingdom, which he gradually enlarged (Gen. 10:8-10).

places.name: Nod
places.summary: Exile; wandering; unrest, a name given to the country to which Cain fled (Gen. 4:16).

places.name: Nodab
places.summary: Noble, probably a tribe descended from one of the sons of Ishmael, with whom the trans-Jordanic tribes made war (1 Chr. 5:19).

places.name: Nophah
places.summary: Blast, a city of Moab which was occupied by the Amorites (Num. 21:30).

places.name: old gate
places.summary: One of the gates in the north wall of Jerusalem, so called because built by the Jebusites (Neh. 3:6; 12:39).

places.name: Ophni
places.summary: Mouldy, a city of Benjamin (Josh. 18:24).

places.name: Paddan
places.summary: A plain, occurring only in Gen. 48:7, where it designates Padan-aram.

places.name: Parah
places.summary: The heifer, a town in Benjamin (Josh. 18:23), supposed to be identical with the ruins called Far’ah, about 6 miles north-east of Jerusalem, in the Wady Far’ah, which is a branch of the Wady Kelt.

places.name: Parbar
places.summary: Added from Digital Manna places-1275 (LPF sync 2026-10-13)

places.name: Parvaim
places.summary: The name of a country from which Solomon obtained gold for the temple (2 Chr. 3:6). Some have identified it with Ophir, but it is uncertain whether it is even the name of a place.

places.name: Pas-dammim
places.summary: The border of blood = Ephes-dammim, between Shochoh and Azekah (1 Sam. 17:1; 1 Chr. 11:13).

places.name: Patara
places.summary: A city on the south-west coast of Lycia at which Paul landed on his return from his third missionary journey (Acts 21:1, 2). Here he found a larger vessel, which was about to sail across the open sea to the coast of Phoenicia.

places.name: Patmos
places.summary: A small rocky and barren island, one of the group called the “Sporades,” in the AEgean Sea. It is mentioned in Scripture only in Rev. 1:9. It was on this island, to which John was banished by the emperor Domitian (A.D. 95), that he received from God the wondrous revelation recorded in his book.

places.name: Pau
places.summary: (Gen. 36:39) or Pai (1 Chr. 1:50), bleating, an Edomitish city ruled over by Hadar.

places.name: Pavement
places.summary: It was the custom of the Roman governors to erect their tribunals in open places, as the market-place, the circus, or even the highway. Pilate caused his seat of judgment to be set down in a place called “the Pavement” (John 19:13) i.e., a place paved with a mosaic of coloured stones.

places.name: Perez-uzza
places.summary: The breach of Uzzah, a place where God “burst forth upon Uzzah, so that he died,” when he rashly “took hold” of the ark (2 Sam. 6:6-8).

places.name: Perez-uzzah
places.summary: The breach of Uzzah, a place where God “burst forth upon Uzzah, so that he died,” when he rashly “took hold” of the ark (2 Sam. 6:6-8).

places.name: Pharpar
places.summary: Swift, one of the rivers of Damascus (2 Kings 5:12). It has been identified with the ‘Awaj, “a small lively river.” The whole of the district watered by the ‘Awaj is called the Wady el-‘Ajam, i.e., “the valley of the Persians”, so called for some unknown reason.

places.name: Phenice
places.summary: Properly Phoenix a palm-tree (as in the R.V.), a town with a harbour on the southern side of Crete (Acts 27:12), west of the Fair Havens.

places.name: Pi-beseth
places.summary: (Ezek. 30:17), supposed to mean. “a cat,” or a deity in the form of a cat, worshipped by the Egyptians. It was called by the Greeks Bubastis.

places.name: Pison
places.summary: Babylonian, the current, broad-flowing, one of the “four heads” into which the river which watered the garden of Eden was divided (Gen. 2:11).

places.name: Pithom
places.summary: Egyptian, Pa-Tum, “house of Tum,” the sun-god, one of the “treasure” cities built for Pharaoh Rameses II. by the Israelites (Ex. 1:11). It was probably the Patumos of the Greek historian Herodotus.

places.name: plain of Aven
places.summary: In Amos 1:5 it denotes the Syrian Heliopolis, the modern Baalbec.

places.name: Pool
places.summary: Heb. shelah; i.e., “the dart”, Neh. 3:15; with the art. shiloah, “sending,” Isa. 8:6 (comp. 7:3)=Siloam

places.name: Ptolemais
places.summary: A maritime city of Galilee (Acts 21:7).

places.name: Pul
places.summary: A geographical name in Isa. 66:19.

places.name: Puteoli
places.summary: A city on the coast of Campania, on the north shore of a bay running north from the Bay of Naples, at which Paul landed on his way to Rome, from which it was distant 170 miles.

places.name: Raamah
places.summary: A country which traded with Tyre (Ezek. 27:22).

places.name: Racal
places.summary: Traffic, a town in the tribe of Judah, to which David sent presents from the spoils of his enemies (1 Sam. 30:29).

places.name: Rakkath
places.summary: Shore-town, a “fenced city” of the tribe of Naphtali (Josh. 19:35).

places.name: Rakkon
places.summary: A place upon the shore, a town belonging to Dan (Josh. 19:46).

places.name: Ramah
places.summary: A town identified with Rameh, on the border of Asher, about 13 miles south-east of Tyre, “on a solitary hill in the midst of a basin of green fields” (Josh. 19:29).

places.name: Ramah
places.summary: One of the “fenced cities” of Naphtali (Josh. 19:36), on a mountain slope, about seven and a half miles west-south-west of Safed, and 15 miles west of the north end of the Sea of Galilee, the present large and well-built village of Rameh.

places.name: Ramath-lehi
places.summary: Elevation of Lehi, or the jawbone height; i.e., the Ramah of Lehi (Judg. 15:15-17). The phrase “in the jaw,” ver. 19, Authorized Version, is in the margin, also in the Revised Version, “in Lehi.”

places.name: Ramath-mizpeh
places.summary: The height of Mizpeh or of the watch-tower (Josh. 13:26), a place mentioned as one of the limits of Gad. There were two Mizpehs on the east of the Jordan.

places.name: Ramathaim-zophim
places.summary: The two heights of the Zophites or of the watchers (only in 1 Sam. 1:1), “in the land of Zuph” (9:5).

places.name: Ramoth
places.summary: Heights.

places.name: Rehob
places.summary: A town of Asher (Josh. 19:28), to the east of Zidon.

places.name: Rehoboth
places.summary: A well in Gerar dug by Isaac (Gen. 26:22), supposed to be in Wady er-Ruheibeh, about 20 miles south of Beersheba.

places.name: Rehoboth
places.summary: Named among the cities of Asshur (Gen. 10:11).

places.name: Rekem
places.summary: A town of Benjamin (Josh. 18:27).

places.name: Remeth
places.summary: Another form of Ramah or Ramoth (1 Chr. 6:73; Josh. 19:21), and probably also of Jarmuth (Josh. 21:29).

places.name: Rephaim
places.summary: Lofty men; giants, (Gen. 14:5; 2 Sam. 21:16, 18, marg. A.V., Rapha, marg. R.V., Raphah; Deut. 3:13, R.V.; A.V., “giants”).

places.name: Resen
places.summary: Head of the stream; bridle, one of Nimrod’s cities (Gen. 10:12), “between Nineveh and Calah.” It has been supposed that the four cities named in this verse were afterwards combined into one under the name of Nineveh.

places.name: Rhegium
places.summary: Breach, a town in the south of Italy, on the Strait of Messina, at which Paul touched on his way to Rome (Acts 28:13).

places.name: Rhodes
places.summary: A rose, an island to the south of the western extremity of Asia Minor, between Coos and Patara, about 46 miles long and 18 miles broad.

places.name: Riblah
places.summary: Fruitful, an ancient town on the northern frontier of Palestine, 35 miles north-east of Baalbec, and 10 or 12 south of Lake Homs, on the eastern bank of the Orontes, in a wide and fertile plain.

places.name: Rumah
places.summary: Elevation, probably the same as Arumah (Judg. 9:41; 2 Kings 23:36), near Shechem.

places.name: Salamis
places.summary: A city on the south-east coast of Cyprus (Acts 13:5), where Saul and Barnabas, on their first missionary journey, preached the word in one of the Jewish synagogues, of which there seem to have been several in that place.

places.name: Salim
places.summary: Peaceful, a place near AEnon, on the west of Jordan, where John baptized (John 3:23).

places.name: Salmone
places.summary: A promontory on the east of Crete, under which Paul sailed on his voyage to Rome (Acts 27:7); the modern Cape Sidero.

places.name: Salt
places.summary: One of the cities of Judah (Josh. 15:62), probably in the Valley of Salt, at the southern end of the Dead Sea.

places.name: Samos
places.summary: An island in the AEgean Sea, which Paul passed on his voyage from Assos to Miletus (Acts 20:15), on his third missionary journey.

places.name: Samothrace
places.summary: An island in the AEgean Sea, off the coast of Thracia, about 32 miles distant. This Thracian Samos was passed by Paul on his voyage from Troas to Neapolis (Acts 16:11) on his first missionary journey.

places.name: Sansannah
places.summary: A palm branch, or a thorn bush, a town in the south (the negeb) of Judah (Josh. 15:31); called also Hazarsusah (19:5), or Hazar-susim (1 Chr. 4:31).

places.name: sea of Jazer
places.summary: water

places.name: sea of the Philistines
places.summary: water

places.name: Secacah
places.summary: Enclosure, one of the six cities in the wilderness of Judah, noted for its “great cistern” (Josh. 15:61).

places.name: Secu
places.summary: A hill or watch-tower, a place between Gibeah and Ramah noted for its “great well” (1 Sam. 19:22); probably the modern Suweikeh, south of Beeroth.

places.name: Seirah
places.summary: Woody district; shaggy, a place among the mountains of Ephraim, bordering on Benjamin, to which Ehud fled after he had assassinated Eglon at Jericho (Judg. 3:26, 27).

places.name: Seleucia
places.summary: The sea-port of Antioch, near the mouth of the Orontes. Paul and his companions sailed from this port on their first missionary journey (Acts 13:4).

places.name: Seneh
places.summary: The acacia; rock-thorn, the southern cliff in the Wady es-Suweinit, a valley south of Michmash, which Jonathan climbed with his armour-bearer (1 Sam. 14:4, 5).

places.name: Sephar
places.summary: Numbering, (Gen. 10:30), supposed by some to be the ancient Himyaritic capital, “Shaphar,” Zaphar, on the Indian Ocean, between the Persian Gulf and the Red Sea.

places.name: Sepharad
places.summary: (Obad. 1:20), some locality unknown. The modern Jews think that Spain is meant, and hence they designate the Spanish Jews “Sephardim,” as they do the German Jews by the name “Ashkenazim,” because the rabbis call Germany Ashkenaz.

places.name: Serpent's Stone
places.summary: The serpent-stone, a rocky plateau near the centre of the village of Siloam, and near the fountain of En-rogel, to which the women of the village resort for water (1 Kings 1:5-9).

places.name: Shaalabbin
places.summary: Or Shaal’bim, a place of foxes, a town of the tribe of Dan (Josh. 19:42; Judg. 1:35). It was one of the chief towns from which Solomon drew his supplies (1 Kings 4:9).

places.name: Shaalim
places.summary: Land of foxes, a place apparently to the north-west of Jerusalem (1 Sam. 9:4), perhaps in the neighbourhood of Shaalabbin in Dan (Josh. 19:42).

places.name: Shaaraim
places.summary: A town in Simeon (1 Chr. 4:31).

places.name: Shalishah
places.summary: Probably the district of Baal-shalisha (2 Kings 4:42), lying about 12 miles north of Lydda (1 Sam. 9:4).

places.name: Shallecheth
places.summary: I.e., “the gate of casting out,” hence supposed to be the refuse gate; one of the gates of the house of the Lord, “by the causeway of the going up” i.e., the causeway rising up from the Tyropoeon valley = valley of the cheesemakers (1 Chr. 26:16).

places.name: Shamir
places.summary: A town among the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:48); probably Somerah, 2 1/2 miles north-west of Debir.

places.name: Shaphir
places.summary: Beautiful, a town of Judah (Micah 1:11), identified with es-Suafir, 5 miles south-east of Ashdod.

places.name: Sharuhen
places.summary: now Tel Sharuhen

places.name: Shaveh-kiriathaim
places.summary: Plain of Kirja-thaim where Chedorlaomer defeated the Emims, the original inhabitants (Gen. 14:5).

places.name: Shebarim
places.summary: Breaks; ruins, a place near Ai (Josh. 7:5; R.V. marg., “the quarries”).

places.name: Shema
places.summary: A town in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:26); the same as Sheba (ver. 5).

places.name: Shen
places.summary: A tooth, probably some conspicuous tooth-shaped rock or crag (1 Sam. 7:12), a place between which and Mizpeh Samuel set up his “Ebenezer.” In the Hebrew the word has the article prefixed, “the Shen.”

places.name: Shihor-libnath
places.summary: Black-white, a stream on the borders of Asher, probably the modern Nahr Zerka, i.e., the “crocodile brook,” or “blue river”, which rises in the Carmel range and enters the Mediterranean a little to the north of Caesarea (Josh. 19:26).

places.name: Shilhim
places.summary: Aqueducts, a town in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:32); called also Sharuhen and Shaaraim (19:6).

places.name: Shimron-meron
places.summary: The same, probably, as Shimron (Josh. 12:20).

places.name: Shion
places.summary: Overturning, a town of Issachar (Josh. 19:19).

places.name: Shoa
places.summary: Opulent, the mountain district lying to the north-east of Babylonia, anciently the land of the Guti, or Kuti, the modern Kurdistan. The plain lying between these mountains and the Tigris was called su-Edina, i.e., “the border of the plain.”

places.name: Shual
places.summary: Land of the fox, a district in the tribe of Benjamin (1 Sam. 13:17); possibly the same as Shalim (9:4), in the neighbourhood of Shaalabbin (Josh. 19:42).

places.name: Silla
places.summary: A highway; a twig, only in 2 Kings 12:20.

places.name: Siphmoth
places.summary: Fruitful places, some unknown place in the south, where David found friends when he fled from Saul (1 Sam. 30:28).

places.name: Sirah
places.summary: Retiring, a well from which Joab’s messenger brought back Abner (2 Sam. 3:26).

places.name: Sitnah
places.summary: Strife, the second of the two wells dug by Isaac, whose servants here contended with the Philistines (Gen. 26:21).

places.name: Skull
places.summary: Only in Luke 23:33, the Latin name Calvaria, which was used as a translation of the Greek word Kranion, by which the Hebrew word Gulgoleth was interpreted, “the place of a skull.”

places.name: Straight Gate
places.summary: The street called “Straight” at Damascus (Acts 9:11) is “a long broad street, running from east to west, about a mile in length, and forming the principal thoroughfare in the city.”

places.name: Suph
places.summary: (Deut. 1:1, R.V.; marg., “some ancient versions have the Red Sea,” as in the A.V.). Some identify it with Suphah (Num. 21:14, marg., A.V.) as probably the name of a place.

places.name: Suphah
places.summary: (Num. 21:14, marg.; also R.V.), a place at the south-eastern corner of the Dead Sea, the Ghor es-Safieh.

places.name: Sychar
places.summary: Liar or drunkard (see Isa. 28:1, 7), has been from the time of the Crusaders usually identified with Sychem or Shechem (John 4:5).

places.name: Syracuse
places.summary: A city on the south-east coast of Sicily, where Paul landed and remained three days when on his way to Rome (Acts 28:12). It was distinguished for its magnitude and splendour.

places.name: Syrtis
places.summary: Found only in Acts 27:17, the rendering of the Greek Syrtis. On the north coast of Africa were two localities dangerous to sailors, called the Greater and Lesser Syrtis.

places.name: Taanath-shiloh
places.summary: Approach to Shiloh, a place on the border of Ephraim (Josh. 16:6), probably the modern T’ana, a ruin 7 miles south-east of Shechem, on the ridge east of the Mukhnah plain.

places.name: Tabbath
places.summary: Famous, a town in the tribe of Ephraim (Judg. 7:22), to the south of Bethshean, near the Jordan.

places.name: Tabor
places.summary: A town of Zebulum (1 Chr. 6:77).

places.name: Tabor
places.summary: The “plain of Tabor” (1 Sam. 10:3) should be, as in the Revised Version, “the oak of Tabor.”

places.name: Tadmor
places.summary: Palm, a city built by Solomon “in the wilderness” (2 Chr. 8:4). In 1 Kings 9:18, where the word occurs in the Authorized Version, the Hebrew text and the Revised Version read “Tamar,” which is properly a city on the southern border of Palestine and toward the wilderness (comp. Ezek. 47:19; 48:28).

places.name: Tappuah
places.summary: A town in the valley or lowland of Judah; formerly a royal city of the Canaanites (Josh. 12:17; 15:34).

places.name: Tel-abib
places.summary: Hill of corn, a place on the river Chebar, the residence of Ezekiel (Ezek. 3:15).

places.name: Telaim
places.summary: Young lambs, a place at which Saul gathered his army to fight against Amalek (1 Sam. 15:4); probably the same as Telem (2).

places.name: Telem
places.summary: A town in the southern border of Judah (Josh. 15:24); probably the same as Telaim.

places.name: Three Taverns
places.summary: A place on the great “Appian Way,” about 11 miles from Rome, designed for the reception of travellers, as the name indicates. Here Paul, on his way to Rome, was met by a band of Roman Christians (Acts 28:15).

places.name: Tiberias
places.summary: A city, the modern Tubarich, on the western shore of the Sea of Tiberias. It is said to have been founded by Herod Antipas (A.D. 16), on the site of the ruins of an older city called Rakkath, and to have been thus named by him after the Emperor Tiberius.

places.name: Timnah
places.summary: A city in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:57)= Tibna near Jeba’.

places.name: Timnath-heres
places.summary: Portion of the sun, where Joshua was buried (Judg. 2:9). It was “in the mount of Ephraim, in the north side of the hill Gaash,” 10 miles south-west of Shechem.

places.name: Tiphsah
places.summary: Passing over; ford, one of the boundaries of Solomon’s dominions (1 Kings 4:24), probably “Thapsacus, a great and wealthy town on the western bank of the Euphrates,” about 100 miles north-east of Tadmor.

places.name: Tiphsah
places.summary: Passing over; ford, one of the boundaries of Solomon’s dominions (1 Kings 4:24), probably “Thapsacus, a great and wealthy town on the western bank of the Euphrates,” about 100 miles north-east of Tadmor.

places.name: Tishbe
places.summary: Elijah the prophet was thus named (1 Kings 17:1; 21:17, 28, etc.). In 1 Kings 17:1 the word rendered “inhabitants” is in the original the same as that rendered “Tishbite,” hence that verse may be read as in the LXX., “Elijah the Tishbite of Tishbi in Gilead.”

places.name: Tochen
places.summary: Measured, a town of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:32).

places.name: Tolad
places.summary: Productive, a town of Simeon, in the south of Judah (1 Chr. 4:29).

places.name: Tophel
places.summary: Lime, a place in the wilderness of Sinai (Deut. 1:1), now identified with Tafyleh or Tufileh, on the west side of the Edomitish mountains.

places.name: Trachonitis
places.summary: A rugged region, corresponds to the Heb. Argob, the Greek name of a region on the east of Jordan (Luke 3:1); one of the five Roman provinces into which that district was divided.

places.name: Trogyllium
places.summary: A town on the western coast of Asia Minor, where Paul “tarried” when on his way from Assos to Miletus, on his third missionary journey (Acts 20:15).

places.name: Ummah
places.summary: Vicinity, a town of Asher (Josh. 19:30).

places.name: Uzal
places.summary: A wanderer, a descendant of Joktan (Gen. 10:27; 1 Chr. 1:21), the founder apparently of one of the Arab tribes; the name also probably of the province they occupied and of their chief city.

places.name: Uzzen-sheerah
places.summary: A town probably near Beth-horon.

places.name: valley of Aijalon
places.summary: A town and valley originally assigned to the tribe of Dan, from which, however, they could not drive the Amorites (Judg. 1:35). It was one of the Levitical cities given to the Kohathites (1 Chr. 6:69).

places.name: valley of Baca
places.summary: (Ps. 84:6; R.V., “valley of weeping,” marg., “or balsam trees”), probably a valley in some part of Palestine, or generally some one of the valleys through which pilgrims had to pass on their way to the sanctuary of Jehovah on Zion; or it may be figuratively “a valley of weeping.”

places.name: valley of Beracah
places.summary: A valley not far from Engedi, where Jehoshaphat overthrew the Moabites and Ammonites (2 Chr. 20:26). It has been identified with the valley of Bereikut.

places.name: valley of Sorek
places.summary: Choice vine, the name of a valley, i.e., a torrent-bed, now the Wady Surar, “valley of the fertile spot,” which drains the western Judean hills, and flowing by Makkedah and Jabneel, falls into the sea some eight miles south of Joppa.

places.name: valley of Zeboim
places.summary: A valley or rugged glen somewhere near Gibeah in Benjamin (1 Sam. 13:18).

places.name: valley of Zered
places.summary: Zared, luxuriance; willow bush, a brook or valley communicating with the Dead Sea near its southern extremity (Num. 21:12; Deut. 2:14). It is called the “brook of the willows” (Isa. 15:7) and the “river of the wilderness” (Amos 6:14).

places.name: way of holiness
places.summary: road

places.name: Yiron
places.summary: now Yaroun

places.name: Zaanan
places.summary: Place of flocks, mentioned only in Micah 1:11.

places.name: Zair
places.summary: Little, a place probably east of the Dead Sea, where Joram discomfited the host of Edom who had revolted from him (2 Kings 8:21).

places.name: Salmon
places.summary: A wood near Shechem, from which Abimelech and his party brought boughs and “put them to the hold” of Shechem, “and set the hold on fire” (Judg. 9:48).

places.name: Zanoah
places.summary: A town in the hill country of Judah, some 10 miles to the south-west of Hebron (Josh. 15:56).

places.name: Zeboim
places.summary: A place mentioned only in Neh. 11:34, inhabited by the Benjamites after the Captivity.

places.name: Zemaraim
places.summary: A town of Benjamin (Josh. 18:22); now the ruin, rather two ruins, es-Sumrah, 4 miles north of Jericho.

places.name: Zephath
places.summary: Beacon; watch-tower, a Canaanite town; called also Hormah, Judg. 1:17.

places.name: Zeredah
places.summary: The fortress, a city on the north of Mount Ephraim; the birthplace of Jeroboam (1 Kings 11:26).

places.name: Zeredah
places.summary: A place in the plain of Jordan; the same as Zarthan (2 Chr. 4:17; 1 Kings 7:46).

places.name: Zererah
places.summary: (Judg. 7:22), perhaps identical with Zereda or Zeredathah.

places.name: Ziddim
places.summary: Sides, a town of Naphtali (Josh. 19:35), has been identified with Kefr-Hattin, the “village of the Hittites,” about 5 miles west of Tiberias.

places.name: Zior
places.summary: Littleness, a city in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:54); the modern Si’air, 4 1/2 miles north-north-east of Hebron.

places.name: Ziph
places.summary: A city in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:24), probably at the pass of Sufah.

places.name: Ziphron
places.summary: Sweet odour, a city on the northern border of Palestine (Num. 34:9), south-east of Hamath.

places.name: Ziz
places.summary: Projecting; a flower, a cleft or pass, probably that near En-gedi, which leads up from the Dead Sea (2 Chr. 20:16) in the direction of Tekoa; now Tell Hasasah.

places.name: Zobah-Hamath
places.summary: Fortress of Zobah, (2 Chr. 8:3) is supposed by some to be a different place from the foregoing; but this is quite uncertain.

places.name: Zophim
places.summary: Field of watchers, a place in Moab on the range of Pisgah (Num. 23:14). To this place Balak brought Balaam, that he might from thence curse the children of Israel.

places.name: Zuph
places.summary: (1 Sam. 9:5, 6), a district in which lay Samuel’s city, Ramah.

places.name: Aram-naharaim
places.summary: Aram of the two rivers, is Mesopotamia (as it is rendered in Gen. 24:10), the country enclosed between the Tigris on the east and the Euphrates on the west (Ps. 60, title); called also the “field of Aram” (Hos. 12:12, R.V.) i.e., the open country of Aram; in the Authorized Version, “country of Syria.”

places.name: Aram-zobah
places.summary: (Ps. 60, title), probably the region between the Euphrates and the Orontes.

places.name: Ashdod's
places.summary: Stronghold, a Philistine city (Josh. 15:47), about midway between Gaza and Joppa, and 3 miles from the Mediterranean. It was one of the chief seats of the worship of Dagon (1 Sam. 5:5).

places.name: Ham
places.summary: Warm, hot, and hence the south; also an Egyptian word meaning “black”, the youngest son of Noah (Gen. 5:32; comp. 9:22, 24).

places.name: Jerusalem's
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Samaria's
places.summary: A watch-mountain or a watch-tower. In the heart of the mountains of Israel, a few miles north-west of Shechem, stands the “hill of Shomeron,” a solitary mountain, a great “mamelon.”

places.name: Zion's
places.summary: Sunny; height, one of the eminences on which Jerusalem was built. It was surrounded on all sides, except the north, by deep valleys, that of the Tyropoeon separating it from Moriah, which it surpasses in height by 105 feet.

events.title: Creation of all things
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 1:1–2:3. People: God, Jesus, Holy Spirit. Lasted about 7 days.

events.title: Creation of Adam and Eve
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 2:4–25. People: Adam, Eve, God. Place: Eden.

events.title: The Fall
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 3:1–24. People: Adam, Eve, God. Place: Eden.

events.title: Cain kills Abel
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 4:1–10. People: Cain, Abel. Place: Eden.

events.title: God curses Cain
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 4:11–16. People: Cain, God. Place: Eden, Nod.

events.title: Birth of Seth
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 4:25 – Luke 3:38. People: Seth, Adam, Eve. Place: Eden.

events.title: Birth of Enos
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 4:26 – 1 Chronicles 1:1. People: Enos, Seth.

events.title: Lifetime of Adam
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 5:3–5. People: Adam. Place: Eden. Lasted about 930 years.

events.title: Death of Adam
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 5:5. People: Adam. Place: Eden.

events.title: Lifetime of Seth
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 5:6–8. People: Seth. Lasted about 912 years.

events.title: Death of Seth
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 5:8. People: Seth.

events.title: Lifetime of Enos
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 5:9–11. People: Enos. Lasted about 905 years.

events.title: Birth of Cainan
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 5:9 – Luke 3:37. People: Cainan, Enos.

events.title: Death of Enos
events.summary: Passage: Genesis 5:11. People: Enos.

events.title: Lifetime of Cainan
